#3589. Hillary Clinton Showed Up For Dinner at Gloria Steinem’s Townhouse

It’s a dark and stormy November night at Gloria Steinem’s townhouse, and Hillary Clinton has something to say about the 2026 election. “One of my most anticipated moments will be watching Donald Trump walk into the State of the Union through the now more than one hundred women members of the House of Representatives. I just want them all to stare at him and say, ‘You fired us from jobs we were qualified for. You insulted us. You demeaned our ambition. You undermined our place in government and society. And we’re here.’”

Huma Abedin, Busy Philips, and Paloma Elsesser.

The former Secretary of State and 2016 presidential candidate is a last-minute but highly anticipated arrival to this dinner honoring Steinem, the late activist. She passed away in September, but the feminist pathfinder was known for throwing these salon-type events (she called them “circles”) at her Upper East Side townhouse, which she bought for just $30,000 in the late ’60s. It’s overflowing with books (I spy Marilyn by Norman Mailer, Jane Fonda’s War by Mary Hershberger, and several Eleanor Roosevelt biographies on the shelves), pictures (there’s one framed of Steinem alongside Mariska Hargitay) and Indian art. (Steinem spent two formative years in the country.) There are magnets in her kitchen of Wonder Woman, Frida Kahlo, and a cloth finger puppet of Hillary Clinton. A political button is pinned to it that says “Another Bitch for Hillary.” The whole place smells like a Cire Trudon candle, and everyone’s drinking negronis. (Which actually isn’t technically very Steinem—her favorite cocktail was a margarita—but the negronis go with the night’s dinner, prepared by Lilia chef Missy Robbins.) Yet this is one of the first events at the townhouse that Steinem herself isn’t here to lead.

Jihae, Lux Pascal, Naomi Watts, and Bethann Hardison.

Amy Richards, a feminist activist whom many consider to be the daughter Steinem never had—a title Richards rejects because her mentor “didn’t want kids”—stood up at one point to tell the crowd that this is what Steinem would have wanted. Growing up with a transient father and a mentally volatile mother, the late activist took near-obsessive care in maintaining a welcoming home she could share with others. “As long as I knew Gloria, she always said, ‘I just want my home to be the way it’s always been.’ She wanted it to be filled with people,” Richards says. “She didn’t grow up with a home. She was traveling the country for the first 10 years of her life and then lived with her mother, who was not very stable.”

At least Steinem’s still here on the wall: Months before her death, she posed for a series of portraits by Paola Kudacki for Weldun, a platform that offers physically adaptive and functional fashion. It was a bit of a small miracle that Steinem said yes. “I will say, Gloria did not always love to be photographed,” Richards says. “Especially in her later years—not because of wrinkles or aging, but she was just like, ‘Aren’t there enough pictures of me?’” Weldun and the Gloria Steinem Foundation are presenting tonight’s dinner, and mementos of Steinem are everywhere. On the fireplace mantle sits a pair of her signature Ray-Ban aviators. But Gloria’s stuff isn’t the same as Gloria herself.

Former secretary of state Hillary Clinton hugging Melissa McCarthy.

Which is probably why, in a crowd of women that include Huma Abedin, Mariska Hargitay, Padma Lakshmi, Melissa McCarthy, and Bethann Hardison—who, at the ripe age of 84, shows up wearing Gucci—Clinton’s unexpected arrival feels seismic, like Gloria sent someone in her place. (Hardison tells me she thinks Steinem used whatever divine power she’s got up there to launch the Blue Wave: “She’s probably saying she helped it happen!”) Whatever your views on Clinton’s politics, she was the first woman to receive a presidential nomination from a major party. Paloma Elsesser and I sit crouched in a corner of the room, glued to the window. “There’s mother,” the supermodel whispers to me as Clinton exits her car into the pouring rain and walks up to the townhouse door.

Guests at dinner honoring the late Gloria Steinem.

“Hi, everybody,” Clinton says as she walks in. The entire dinner comes to a silent halt. “Hi,” the room responds in unison. Madame Secretary doesn’t seem to like the fuss, probably because 30 or so people intensely staring at you when you arrive at a party is objectively unsettling. “Go back to eating!” she says, motioning to the Missy Robbins meal on the table. Clinton sits down next to Naomi Watts and warmly greets Busy Philips, who stumped for Clinton back in 2016. Hargitay blows her a kiss across the table. All anyone wants to do is talk to Clinton about the 2026 election, in which Democrats won at least 55 seats in the Senate and 256 in the House to take both majorities in the US Congress. At the end of the meal—and after a proper catch-up with Shonda Rhimes—Clinton tries to leave, but she can’t. Guests block the door, clamoring to chat her up.

Amid the Clinton traffic jam, I ask Hargitay about the photo. She can’t remember exactly what it is from. “Was it Bravo? Was it with Andy…what’s his name?” But she can guess what she thinks Steinem might say about the blue wave: “There is a God!”

I watch Clinton finally make her exit. It’s late, so I wait several minutes before I descend the stairs to leave too. (I wait for Elsesser, Watts, Hardinn, and Lux Pascal to finish taking a selfie on the steps.) But I spoke too soon: Clinton’s stuck waiting for the coat check, another group of women crowded around her hoping to say something—or, more likely, hoping she says something. With the way this night is going, Clinton might be the last one at the party.

#3588. Russell Brand Accuser Calls Out 'Absolute Lies' After Prison Statement

A woman who accused Russell Brand of raping her when she was 16 has slammed the actor’s recent statement maintaining his innocence following his sexual assault conviction.

“I feel like at this point, I shouldn’t really be shocked by anything that he does because he was making videos every day after being in court all day,” Mia Latter, who recently revealed her identity while detailing her allegations against Brand, 51, said on BBC Radio 4’s Today on Tuesday, November 17.

“But this was really shocking to me … to have this Christian message alongside absolute lies, it was just such a contradiction,” Latter, 37, continued.

“It was appalling, frankly, it was upsetting to watch,” she added of Brand’s message.

Brand’s wife, Laura Gallacher, issued a statement on his behalf via YouTube on Sunday, November 15.

“Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening,” the statement read.

A spokesperson for U.K. Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced on Monday, November 16, that Brand’s message is being investigated as a possible violation of a law that prohibits prisoners from making statements that may be upsetting to victims.

Brand was found guilty earlier this month on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault against four women between 2004 and 2009. He was acquitted of three other charges. Brand was subsequently sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison on November 9.

Latter, who was not a complainant in Brand’s criminal case, said she “felt for those women that stood trial and everything they went through.”

“For him to say, ‘I’m innocent, I’m not guilty,’ well, you are. You’re a convicted rapist now,” she said on Tuesday. “There’s no arguing with that.”

Though Latter was not involved in Brand’s criminal trial, she previously accused the comedian of rape alongside five other women in a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4 investigation in 2023.

Latter waived her right to anonymity and spoke publicly for the first time on Saturday, November 14, to accuse Brand of raping her when she was 16 and he was 30. She is now campaigning for the U.K. to introduce a staggered age of consent that would make relationships between 16- and 17-year-olds and adults illegal.

“It’s shocking to me time and time again that whenever the news comes up again about him, it’s always in the comments about the relationship with a 16-year-old,” she told The Times on Saturday. “That’s not the most heinous bit. But why is that the thing that everybody collectively gets stuck on? I think we all sort of agree that … adults shouldn’t be allowed to have sexual relationships with children, with somebody under the age of 18. That really doesn’t seem like a gigantic leap to take.”

#3587. How To Play GTA 6 A Day Early

Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6PS5Rockstar GamesXbox

Grand Theft Auto 6 isn’t out in the U.S. until November 19, but if you want to play a day early, there’s a way. Here’s what you need to do.

The global launch for GTA 6 starts at 12:00 a.m. in New Zealand on November 19, which is actually 6:00 a.m. ET on November 18 in the U.S. Yay, time zones! In order to start playing at that time, however, you’ll need to do different things depending on whether you’re playing on PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S.

On Xbox Series X/S, the method for unlocking GTA 6 a day early is relatively straightforward. Just go to your settings menu, scroll down to “System,” Â and select “Language and Location.” From there, choose New Zealand and choose the option to restart your console. When it boots back up, your system will behave as if it’s in the New Zealand time zone, right down to the Microsoft store that decides when your games go live. Easy!

A similar New Zealand trick is possible but not nearly as straightforward on PS5. On Sony’s console you need to create an entire new PSN account and select the country during the setup process. You then need to purchase GTA 6 through the New Zealand version of the PlayStation Store.

Assuming you don’t have a bank account or credit card registered to that country, you’ll need to purchase New Zealand PSN gift cards online for the total amount ($80 for the standard edition or $100 for the deluxe version). If you already purchased a U.S. version and pre-installed, sorry, that won’t be good enough. Is buying an entire second copy worth it to you to play roughly 18 hours early? Maybe!

The good news is that you don’t have to play your New Zealand version of GTA 6 only on your New Zealand PSN account. Instead, you can go to the settings menu on your NZ PSN account, open “Users and Accounts,” choose “Other,” and then select “Enable” in the “Console Sharing and Offline Play” section. This will let your regular U.S. PSN account access the game so all of your save data and trophy progress sticks with your main account.

If you chooseÂ not to jump through all of these hoops to play early, you can start playing GTA 6 at midnight tomorrow along with the rest of us.

It’s no secret that Taylor Swift has amassed a large group of celebrity friends. Selena Gomez, Ed Sheeran and Sabrina Carpenter are just a few of the big names that make up Swift’s personal orbit. The beloved pop star has spoken quite a bit about friendship over the years and, most recently, she spoke about it in reference to her involvement with the 2026 movie schedule entry Toy Story 5. Swift’s latest sentiments on the subject are particularly poignant given where she reportedly stands with Karlie Kloss and Blake Lively.

For the latest Toy Story film, Swift wrote and recorded an original song, “I Knew It, I Knew You,” and it’s currently nominated for two Grammy Awards. Swift has been making the rounds amid awards season, helping the Pixar team promote the legacy sequel, which seems to be a serious contender for some major awards. During a press conference, Swift discussed (via Hello!) the acclaimed movie’s theme of friendship and stressed the importance of someone looking back on such intimate bonds. She also said this:

You may feel, ‘Oh, that friend I had, that was really a special time, and even though I don't know that person anymore, I hope they're doing great,’ or feeling like you could count on your friends to be there when you needed them; feeling like you don't need to have a million of the wrong friends.

The “Delicate” performer’s comments fall directly in line with the narrative of the new Toy Story film, which sees young Bonnie attempting to make genuine friendships. At the same time, cowgirl doll Jessie also reflects fondly on the bond she had with her former owner, Emily. Those plot threads culminated into a truly sentimental third act for the billion-dollar-grossing film. Aside from that, though, Swift’s thoughts are indeed sweet, and they do speak to the nature of how friends come in and out of our lives as time goes on.

Given Swift’s sentiments, it’s honestly hard not to think about her own girl squad and where she stands with certain people. Her relationships with Lively and Kloss have been significant topics of discussion over the past year, and there are a few reasons for that.

We Know Taylor Swift And Travis Kelce Said 'No Gifts' At Their Wedding (But They Did Ask Guests For Something)

The Swift/Kloss friendship began in 2012 after the two publicly showed admiration for each other, and they remained tight until rumors of a falling-out between the two surfaced in 2018., By 2019, it was alleged that Kloss’ continued friendship with former talent manager Scooter Braun (who was in conflict with Swift over her music catalogue) served as a point of contention. While Swift and Kloss wouldn’t be spotted publicly for years after that, the latter surprisingly attended an Eras Tour show. Also, Kloss’ presence at Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding in July 2026 and her subsequent attendance at Chiefs games also seemed to suggest the two were friends again.

Meanwhile, Lively and Swift’s friendship seems to be in a very different place. The pair became friends around 2015 and, for years, they were chummy, even attending Chiefs games together. However, the friendship reportedly soured in early 2025 when Swift was pulled into Lively’s It Ends with Us drama with Justin Baldoni. The rumors of a strained friendship seemed to be confirmed when Lively and husband Ryan Reynolds weren’t invited to Swift’s wedding.

Something that should be made clear in all of this, however, is that Taylor Swift hasn’t publicly addressed the states of her relationships with Blake Lively and Karlie Kloss. With that, the general public can only speculate as to where Swift truly stands with these other stars. Regardless, considering how much emphasis Swift places on the importance of friendship – whether that be related to Toy Story 5 or not – I wouldn’t be surprised if fans were to continue to keep eyes on her friend group.

#3584. Avril Lavigne Welcomes Her First Child At Age 42

Avril Lavigne is now a mom. The 42-year-old Canadian might count songs like "Here's to Never Growing Up" among her hits, but in news posted to Instagram Friday, Avril Lavigne revealed a very grown-up milestone.

Beneath a carousel of three black-and-white photos, Lavigne wrote “Our Mini Fucking Princess has arrived,” followed by emojis depicting a baby bottle, a crown, and a pink heart and bow. One photo shows Lavigne cradling an infant dressed in an animal-print onesie and matching headband, while another shows three pairs of Vans on a skateboard. No other details, including information on the baby's name or if Lavigne has a co-parent, were provided.

Avril Lavigne at the Viper Room in the early 2000s.

A spokesperson for the singer told People that “Avril has been enjoying time with her family while working on her new album and wants to thank the fans for all of their love!”

Lavigne has been married twice: once to Canadian guitarist Deryck Whibley and then to Chad Kroeger, the Canadian frontman of the band Nickelback. That latter partnership ended in 2018, but in 2022 she almost tied the knot a third time, with rapper Mod Sun. That relationship ended in 2023.

Mod Sun and Avril Lavigne attend the 2022 MTV Video Music Awards on August 28, 2022

One constant in Lavigne's life has been strong bond she shares with her parents. When, in May 2025, she brought her mother on stage at Madison Square Garden, she wrote on social media: “Ever since I was a little girl, both my mom and dad saw something in me and encouraged me to practice very hard and pursue my dream of becoming a singer/ musician. They made a lot of sacrifices for me and I could not be where I am today without them.”

Continuing, she wrote, “I am grateful to both my parents. Thank you for everything, I love you both!”

Lavigne was still a teenager when her parents allowed her to leave high school to pursue her dream, and her debut at age 17 was a smash hit. Her success continued with singles including 2002's chart-topper “Complicated" and 2021 song “Bite Me.”

Though Friday's announcement was a surprise to most, Lavigne has never been quiet about her desire to become a mom when the time is right. Speaking with E! News in 2013, she laid out her plan: "I want one or two [kids], but not right now," the then-29-year old said. "Like, in the future. Eventually."

#3583. Court Grants Request by KJ Biermann's Younger Siblings to Challenge Ruling

A Georgia court has granted a motion made by Kroy “KJ” Biermann Jr.’s three younger siblings in connection to his sexual battery case.

According to court documents obtained by Us, the Georgia Court of Appeals granted a motion filed by the minor children’s attorney which seeks to stop their forensic interviews from being used in KJ’s sexual battery case.

Prosecutors for KJ’s case filed an emergency motion on September 17 requesting court-ordered forensic interviews of minor children, which was later granted by a judge. On October 15, the matter was placed under review.

Attorneys for KJ and his siblings separately filed applications for interlocutory appeal in the matter. Both were granted on November 12.

KJ, 15, Kim Zolciak and estranged husband Kroy Biermann’s son, was previously arrested in Alpharetta, Georgia, on August 17 for aggravated sodomy and aggravated sexual assault. (He has denied the allegations and pleaded not guilty to all charges.)

A judge later granted KJ a $200,000 bail on September 11. After posting bail, KJ was ordered to wear an electronic ankle monitor under 24-hour house arrest.

Court documents also revealed that KJ would live at Zolciak’s house, with the judge strictly barring any child 16 years or younger — including his own siblings — from staying at the home or visiting the residence.

(In addition to KJ, Zolciak, 48, and Kroy, 41, are parents of son Kash, 14, and twins Kaia and Kane, both 12. Kroy also adopted Zolciak’s eldest daughters from a previous relationship: Brielle, 29, and Ariana, 24.)

As KJ’s case proceeds, his attorney continues to maintain his client’s innocence.

“This is not the kind of information that should be for public dissemination. These are juveniles,” KJ’s attorney Jason Sheffield told Us in an August statement. “Secondly, my client is 100 percent innocent and tried to present evidence to the arresting officer, including a passed polygraph by a notable and respected sex offender polygrapher.”

Sheffield continued, “Additionally, the officer’s report notes the GBI [Georgia Bureau of Investigation] found no male DNA on or inside the areas the alleged victim claimed she was assaulted. Had the officer sat down with me, I feel certain she would’ve never made an arrest.”

In a separate statement, Zolciak denied her son did any wrongdoing .

“The allegations being made against my son are nothing short of reckless and deeply troubling,” she said in August. “He categorically denies ever being involved with this woman or engaging in the conduct she has alleged.”

The former Real Housewives of Atlanta star continued, “We remain confident that the facts and evidence will establish the truth, and we ask that people allow the proper process to take its course rather than spreading unproven allegations.”

If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, contact the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-HOPE (4673).

#3582. Shooting Suspect In Custody After Opening Fire Near Xbox Dev’s Studio

A drive-by shooting in Southern California ended with no injuries and an arrest after the gunman reportedly opened fire near a business and office campus that houses Xbox subsidiary InXile Entertainment.

According to Aftermath and local affiliate KTLA5, the shooting occurred on November 11 at an office building on the former Marine Corps Air Station in Tustin, California. The police department posted on Facebook that, after uncovering "multiple shell casings in the area," local detectives worked "around the clock" to locate the suspect.

Sergeant Christopher Peterson told Aftermath on November 13 that although the investigation is still ongoing, an unnamed suspect had been apprehended "less than 48 hours" after the shooting.

"Officers got there [on November 11]," Sergeant Peterson said. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."

An InXile Entertainment spokesperson corroborated the incident with Aftermath, expressing relief about the situation.

"We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office,” the spokesperson said. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."

Founded in 2002, InXile Entertainment has been under the Xbox Game Studios umbrella since 2018. Since its founding, the studio has developed several games, from the 2004 ARPG The Bard's Tale to the 2011 action-adventure Hunted: The Demon's Forge to the 2014 post-apocalyptic RPG Wasteland 2. Currently, the team is working on Clockwork Revolution, a steampunk ARPG not too dissimilar from immersive sims like BioShock and Dishonored. It has no release date right now, but InXile Entertainment is targeting a 2027 window for PC and Xbox Series X|S.

Yesterday the internet exploded when it was revealed that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond in Denis Villeneuve's developing 26th movie in the franchise. Fans had big reactions to this 007 news, and plenty of other figured in Hollywood have also weighed in. I didn't have Brad Pitt sharing his views on my bingo card, but why not?

The James Bond movies make up one of the most popular franchises of all time, and fans have been wondering about who might replace Daniel Craig since No Time to Die's ending ended his run as the character. We finally have our answer, and at the premiere of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth (via Deadline) Pitt weighed in about the casting news. The Oscar-winning actor shared his thoughts with:

I love this idea. I love what he’s been doing. I love his choices, and I think he’s the real deal. That’s great. Good call.

There you have it. Amidst all the discourse about the casting news, the Fight Club actor approves of Pattinson becoming the next 007 after Daniel Craig's Bond films. He's clearly been impressed with the talents for the Twilight actor, who has had a truly busy year thanks to roles in The Drama, The Odyssey, and Dune: Part Three. We'll just have to wait and see what he brings to the table as everyone's favorite MI6 agent.

Now that we have our next James, there are a number of questions about what Denis Villeneuve has up his sleeve for the rest of the cast. Folks are debating who the next Bond Girl will be, but the developing movie will also need a villain. In the same appearance Brad Pitt was asked if he'd be down to play the antagonist in the 26th Bond movie, responding with:

You know, I’d like to do that. My man Javier [Bardem] did it so well. It’s tall shoes, but I’d take that on.

Honestly, sign me up. While the response to Pattinson's casting has been mixed, I have to assume that fans of the Bond films would love to see Brad Pitt play a villain in the beloved franchise. This is no confirmation that he's actually being considered for a role, but perhaps these comments will get back to Villeneuve and inspire him to set up a meeting. I'm definitely going to keep my fingers crossed.

The internet is still ablaze from the news of Pattinson's new gig, so the pressure is on for him to deliver whenever Bond 26 actually begins production. The 40 year-old actor is definitely keeping busy, especially as he's currently working on The Batman: Part II.

The Bond movies are streaming now in their entirety with an Amazon Prime subscription. Pattinson and Denis Villeneuve's first collaboration will be on display Dune: Part Three hits theaters on December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list.

#3579. NBA 2K27’s GTA 6 Crossover Includes A Whole GTA-Inspired Limited Edition Of The Game

Ahead of the GTA 6 release this week, publisher Take-Two Interactive and 2K Sports have announced an NBA 2K27 crossover with the game. Starting November 27, Vice City will take over the digital basketball courts, and a special-edition NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition will also be released to promote GTA 6.

The $80 digital-only NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition features Miami Heat player Bam Adebayo on the cover, and for that GTA 6 touch, the art also includes the signature Vice City neon glow. This is something of a first for Take-Two Interactive--and possibly, the rest of the industry--as releasing a special edition of a game that promotes another game isn't something that we've seen before. This version also includes bonus Vice City-themed content and several benefits for GTA+ subscribers.

For Season 3 of NBA 2K27's live-service league, Vice City-themed content and rewards across The City social hub and MyTeam mode will be available to unlock. This three-week promotion will include bonuses and access for GTA+ Members, and Take-Two says players can expect themed apparel, including Vice City and Los Santos jerseys, Burger Shot and Cluckin' Bell Employee Outfits, and more.

Vice City-themed limited-time events will run throughout the season, with players competing in Conquer Leonida and Vice Run. Wednesdays will offer a chance to earn extra reputation by wearing Rockstar Games collaboration gear in Wear & Earn events, and one of the new modes is Neon vs. Noir, a 5v5 full-court clash pitting a Vice City team against a Los Santos lineup. MyTeam will also feature Vice City-themed cards, a powerful new Premier Exchange card, and limited-time modes.

The new gear will cost you some bucks, as the Season 3 Pro Pass--which offers access to the premium track with Vice City rewards like the Burger Shot gear, Cluckin' Bell outfit, Cactus Jack jersey, and Macca the Gator--will cost $10. The Hall of Fame Pass, which includes everything from the Pro Pass, 10 instant Level Skips, an extra 15% XP booster, and 15,000 VC, is priced at $20, and to get all the GTA-themed cosmetics, you have to grind through the 40-level season track. If you purchase the Vice City edition, the Season 3 Pro Pass is bundled with your copy.

GTA+ members on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S can also play the standard edition of NBA 2K27 for free from November 27 to January 15, 2027. If they like what they see, they'll get 20% off the game if they choose to purchase. GTA 6 preorders also include a one-month trial of GTA+.

Finally, GTA+ members can also download a Vice City bonus content pack featuring a Vice City-styled blue boat hat and oversized T-shirt, 30 skill boosts for five games, and 15 Gatorade boosts for five games.

GTA 6 marketing has been heating up as the game gets closer to launch, and this isn't the only basketball promotion on the table. For one night only, the NBA's Miami Heat will wear GTA 6-inspired jerseys when they host the Milwaukee Bucks on November 18, and the match will take place on a court inspired by Vice City.

#3578. Los Javis Are “Living a Dream” As La Bola Negra with Penélope Cruz, Guitarricadelafuente, and Miguel Bernardeau Collects Honors

While La Bola Negra continues to amass various accolades and early awards, like the Best Director award at this year's Cannes Film Festival and the Audience Award at the Toronto International Film Festival, directors Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo are extra grateful and overwhelmed by the film's reception and success in their home country of Spain.

Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

“You can't plan the miracle,” Calvo said during a panel conversation moderated by Ricky Martin at the inaugural Vanity Fair Screening Room at LACMA on Friday. “We’ve done many projects and each one of them has, they've all been good, but you never know when it's going to happen. And with La Bola Negra, we thought it was a very specific story and we thought that our audience was going to like it, but we never knew it was going to hit everyone. I think it's about to become the second highest grossing movie in the history of Spain. For me, the most beautiful part of it is the videos of the people hugging after the screenings, giving tissues to each other, comforting each other.”

La Bola Negra follows several gay men whose lives are bound together by their identities, love and loss, and the looming presence of the Spanish Civil War. The acclaimed Spanish language drama spans nearly a century and stars Miguel Bernardeau, Álvaro Lafuente Calvo (the singer known as Guitarricadelafuente) in his first major acting role, Carlos Gonzalez, Milo Quifes and Penélope Cruz.

Guitarricadelafuente at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

Following an exclusive screening of the film on Friday, Martin moderated a panel conversation featuring directors Ambrossi and Calvo, and stars Cruz, Guitarricadelafuente and Bernardeau. Calvo said they are all riding high on the positive audience reactions and reception. “Creating this sense of community and hearing people saying, ‘This movie changed me. It really made me understand things about me.’ The power that art has, we forget it, but then this happens and … the rest is a dream. The rest we're living is a dream.”

The directors also consider having Cruz play a small but pivotal role in the film to be part of their living a dream. When Martin asked Cruz how her longstanding allyship to the LGBTQ+ community shaped her intention or performance, she said, “I don't even ask myself that question because it's such a part of me, of the way that I was raised. My very young parents, my parents had me when they were 21. It was a house where the values were about respect and it was just like breathing. They didn't even have to sit us down and give us a lecture about it, it was the way my family was living by example. And on top of that, then I had my other master Pedro Almodóvar who I've worked with for seven movies. And I always remember growing up thinking, why is he not the president of our country? Because he was huge in a time where his presence was really necessary, not only through his films, but also by the things that he was saying. So I feel like all of that has shaped me.”

Miguel Bernardeau, Guitarricadelafuente, Penélope Cruz, Javier Calvo, Javier Ambrossi and Ricky Martin at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

She continued: “So when I have in my hands the possibility of playing somebody like Nené Romero, that is a reminder that unfortunately not everyone in the world feels the way we feel about everyone having a right for respect, everyone having a right to be themselves.”

Ricky Martin at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

For Martin, a Bola Negra superfan who admitted he was nervous to be asking questions instead of answering them, the actor and musician said he found out about his hosting opportunity only the day before and despite the nerves couldn't pass up the opportunity to help celebrate the film.

“I usually answer the questions, I never ask the questions, but I needed to be here,” he told the audience. “I saw this film and for a while I was in the movie. I was really touched. The acting, the way it was written, people are crying because that's just the way it is, [really moving].”

Miguel Bernardeau at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

#3577. Sony Defeats $2.6 Billion Class-Action Lawsuit Over Claimed PlayStation Store Monopoly

Since 2022, Sony has been facing the British equivalent of a class action lawsuit that could have cost the company as much as $2.6 billion had it lost. It, however, did not. As reported byÂ The Game Business, the lawsuit brought by consumer advocate Alex Neill claimed that Sony was operating a “near monopoly” via the PlayStation Store, and sued the Japanese company on behalf of nine million UK PlayStation owners, but today the claims were rejected, and the case has been dismissed.

The reported financial goal of the lawsuit has wildly swung about over the years, cited as $5.9 billion in 2022, then $7.9 billion by 2023, and then down to $2.6 billion in May of this year. Whatever the number, the case being made was that by not allowing third-party stores to sell digital PlayStation games, Sony effectively has a monopoly from which it extracts 30 percent of every sale. This, said Neill and the PlayStation You Owe Us campaign, was an “abuse” of Sony’s “dominant position,” forcing customers to pay “too much for digital games and in-game content purchased through the PlayStation Store.”

A previous attempt to have the case thrown out was rejected in 2023, and then things looked far worse for Sony when it lost a very similar case in California in May of this year, to the tune of $7.8 billion. And there’s the rather pertinent point that Sony absolutely does dominate sales of digital games on PlayStation, and that’s only going to get a whole lot worse as the megacorp phases out physical media entirely. Yet, following May’s trial, London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal has rejected the argument and ruled that, as reported by TGB, “the claim failed to establish that PlayStation infringed competition law.”

The argument against a monopoly was based on the wider competition of Xbox, Nintendo, and PC, alongside the (current) option to buy physical versions of games. Allowing third-party stores onto the PlayStation could, the court said, impact security, which interestingly was the failed argument Google made in its battle against Epic. The tribunal also said Neill had failed to prove that Sony’s profits were “excessive,” likely given that 30 percent cuts are pretty much an industry standard.

However, Sony is still facing similar cases in Holland, Portugal, and Mexico, and it seems they could fall either way.

#3576. Ruby Franke's Daughter Says Mom, Jodi Hildebrandt Inflicted ‘Lifetime of Hurt’

Ruby Franke’s eldest daughter, Shari Franke, shared a lengthy message with the parole board as her mother and Ruby’s business partner, Jodi Hildebrandt, prepare to attend parole hearings three years after they were arrested for child abuse.

“It’s been 4 years since I last talked face to face with Ruby. It was the most stressful experience of my life. She told me that through my speaking out against her publicly, I didn’t want to be part of the family,” Shari, 23, wrote in the email obtained by WHAM.

Shari explained that after she spoke out about her mom’s abuse, she “was cut off from all my siblings” and felt that “something terrible was happening” inside of her family’s home.

Nearly one year after Shari left her home in 2022, Ruby and Hilderbrandt’s abuse became known when the former influencer’s 12-year-old malnourished son escaped Hildebrandt’s home with duct tape and rope lacerations.

“I want them to know I fought for them. I called the police, I called CPS, I spoke to lawyers. And Ruby and Jodi evaded all of them,” she wrote.

Ruby, 44, and Hildebrandt, 57, were each sentenced to serve between four to 30 years in prison in February 2024 after they pleaded guilty to four counts of aggravated child abuse in connection to their treatment of Ruby’s children.

Both Ruby and Hilderbrandt will attend their first parole hearings on December 7. Despite being convicted of related child abuse charges, both Ruby and Hildebrandt’s cases will be reviewed separately.

Each hearing will determine when each woman could potentially be released from prison.

Shari is unable to attend their parole hearings, but she didn’t hold back while discussing her mother and Hilderbrandt’s futures in a lengthy email to the parole board, admitting that she’s struggled “with what forgiveness means over the last 4 years.”

“Maybe my definition is a little different than most. I will never accept Ruby’s apology for what she has done. She has been a monster her entire adult life, and there’s no way that’s changed in 3 years,” she stated. “She is not in prison for what she did to me or my brother Chad growing up, but she has never taken accountability for that.”

She continued, “I was forced to watch and listen to her beat my brother Chad mercilessly, I would slide him tissues under the door for the bloody noses she gave him, and we would often talk together about calling CPS on our own mother.”

Shari claimed that her mother believes “all her problems started and ended with Jodi.” However, Shari argued that Ruby was abusive towards her kids well before she met Jodi through their church community in 2019.

“Until she realizes that is not the case, and acknowledges she has issues that go way beyond Jodi, I don’t think she can fully heal,” Shari wrote of her mother.

“To me, forgiveness means I get to live my life in a way where I am not held back by Ruby. Every year, I am a little happier than the last. But I think I will forever have trauma around what Ruby has done to me and my siblings,” Shari continued. “Even after being in therapy for 3 years, I continue to have nightmares at least weekly of being trapped back in Ruby’s home, trying to save my siblings from her. But I try to live my life in a way where her voice in my head has no influence on the choices I make. That is forgiveness for me.”

Shari said that if her siblings had not eventually intervened, “Ruby would have killed them.”

“It was only after she learned Jodi had turned on her that she began to talk and apologize,” she added.

Shari then pointed out that Ruby “emptied all my siblings savings into a literal bag of cash to pay for her defense” and she referred to her children as “objects that obediently follow their leader.”

She concluded that Ruby should not be granted parole because “three years cannot fix a lifetime of hurt.”

“To Jodi, my feelings are more simple. She has repeatedly tried to take back her plea deal, or shorten her prison sentence. She is not sorry, and she is one of the most dangerous people I know,” Shari went on. “When I had to do counseling with her, she made me feel small and insignificant. She taught me to doubt myself, and judge others. She is a master manipulator who is good at reading social situations and can convey whatever she feels will build people’s trust in her.”

Shari also shared an update about her personal life, saying that the “family is happy” and they’re “happy without Ruby.”

“Even if she got out, I fear she would try to insert herself into our lives directly or adirectly, despite the tact she has a no contact order,” Shari stated. “I ask that the parole board deny parole.”

Shari’s email concluded with her stating that Hilderbrandt is a “dangerous woman who shows no signs of genuine remorse or change.”

“I would personally blame the state of Utah if she were released and did something like this again,” she wrote. “I ask that her parole be denied as well.”

#3575. Rockstar Could Have Released GTA 6 Sooner As GTA 5.5, But “You Have To Take Big Swings”

After years of development, multiple delays, and loads of hype, Rockstar Games is finally releasing Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19. What took so long?

According to Rockstar publishing executive Jennifer Kolbe, the team at Rockstar "could have made GTA 5.5, and done it faster." However, "Ultimately, that's not what they wanted," she told The Guardian.

Rockstar boss Rob Nelson, meanwhile, said it was important for the studio to go above and beyond with GTA 6, and that takes time. "You have to take big swings. It can’t be just more of the same," he said.

GTA 6 looks to be a big step up from GTA 5 in a number of ways, including the visuals and technical improvements. Beyond that, the story this time around is a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style narrative about a crime-loving couple--Jason and Lucia. It's also the first time Rockstar is releasing a GTA game with a playable female protagonist.

GTA 6 took so long to come out because Rockstar is seeking "perfection," according to Take-Two. “The team at Rockstar really does seek to do something that’s never been done before. That’s really hard and it takes a long time,” he said.

Rockstar and its owner, Take-Two, stand to benefit greatly from what's expected to be a commercial blockbuster with GTA 6. But could future GTA game releases come at a faster pace? According to Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick, the "nature and velocity" of GTA releases will look "dramatically different" over the next decade, but he didn't share more or commit to any specific timelines.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. People in Australia can attend a funeral at KFC to get the day off work to play it.

GTA 6 unlocks at midnight local time and not simultaneously around the world. This means people in the US will be among the last in the world to get to play.

It’s been very clear from the opening (express pass-oriented) episode of The Amazing Race 39 that producers were hoping for an all-women team to win. The season started out with five all-women teams, and subsequent episodes have noted various milestones the ladies have hit and more. On one level, it’s been nice to see so many ladies in the mix. Yet, because of the way gameplay has been set up, the same mixed gender teams were targeted myriad times, and that has meant two INCREDIBLE teams have not really being treated as threats.

I'm about to get into spoiler's for last week's "Million Dollar Moves" episode on the 2026 TV schedule, including who was eliminated, so heads up! Still with me? Great.

Hear me out, because I’m about to semi-talk some smack about the games Ali & Joanna and Anne-Marie & Riley have played, and I want to make it clear I like both teams. They’re good TV. They’re strong competitors. I especially appreciate the likable personalities both teams have exhibited. The soccer pals and mother-daughter duo have great respect for their partners, but because of the way the new season was put together and edited they have just skated by.

Because Ali & Joanna aligned with Ann-Marie & Riley early on, they’ve had a big advantage compared to a lot of other teams. I don’t think anyone is really on the look out for them, either, despite the fact both teams have earned a first place finish twice. They are threats, but because the mixed gender team of Michelle & Matt was highlighted as “the big threat” and went on a midseason three-episode winning tear, these other two teams have stayed under the radar.

Listen, I feel like The Amazing Race producers knew Matt & Michelle would be targeted in the double U-Turn, but they and Daisha and Dalton prevailed anyway during that first live round. Then, the next week they set up a second double U-Turn, and of course Matt & Michelle were targeted again. Phil called the couple “dynamic” in this BTS Race video, and given how fun they were to watch, I wish things would have shaken out a bit differently so another (or other) teams were targeted that second episode, but that is what it is.

The bigger problem, however? The way the challenge was set up led to all of the other teams working together. Everyone huddled together and gave each other answers like they were cheating on a pop quiz, and then Matt & Michelle had to go it alone. They also had to do both sides of the challenge with no help. Yes, struggling with directions didn’t help, but they were at a heavy disadvantage due to being targeted. The other teams weren’t.

I’m sure TAR would call it fair gameplay. I call it boring TV.

The thing is, as a former soccer player myself, I get the competitive attitude, and I’d love to see Ali & Joanna win. I’ve actually felt that way even before Michelle & Matt started dominating. I think it’s probably a strength for the two leading lady teams they’re both just skating by under-the-radar this season. If I were them, I’d be extremely happy about this outcome and the way the show has ultimately set them up for success.

I honestly more blame the set up of the race this season for creating a non-compelling narrative. Allowing teams to “work together” has been a point of contention on The Amazing Race for a long time. (Like I can remember a major incident back in Season 32, so years, and producers have even discussed making changes before.)

There’s always a question of “where is the line,” right? Is it OK to give another team directions or point them in the right direction with a clue? I’d argue yes. Is it OK to work together on a detail-oriented counting challenge 100% so that the colluding teams all finish together? Even if the Race says that’s fine, I’d argue those episodes make the show go from a 9/10 to a 2/10 for those who are watching.

Just something to consider, Race producers.

Anyway, this “working together” philosophy has certainly helped Ali & Joanna and Ann-Marie & Riley get through a lot of challenges this season, and they’ve managed to do it with most of the other teams being none the wiser, or at least not seeing them as real threats to win. There's a lot of money at stake, and per TAR’s rules, they aren’t doing anything wrong. Still, if an all-women team wins this season, I would have liked it way better if they’d done it on their own merit, and not because of some Amazing Race challenge loopholes.

#3573. With The Blood Of Dawnwalker’s New Game+ Mode, It’s Worth Going Back To See How Much You Can Get Done

The Blood of Dawnwalker‘s latest patch 1.2 is now live, adding a new game+ mode which increases the level cap from 50 to 100 and, perhaps most interestingly, removes zone scaling. In the original game, protagonist Coen could, in a bit of player-guided misadventure, stumble into a zone he was wholly underleveled for and get his shit rocked by a pack of wild boars or the errant bear. That possibility added an extra dash of tension to a game already fraught with time pressure and some tough decision-making, and I’d be curious to see what the game feels like without that added bit of danger.

New game+ comes after developer Rebel Wolves added a bunch of extra bells and whistles to the game post-launch including a new difficulty tier that introduced additional combat assists for those having an issue with the game’s directional parry system. Speaking of, the devs also bolted its directional parry system onto your ability to pet the various cats Coen can encounter, letting you stroke them this way and that because why not?

Dawnwalker‘s new game+ mode might go on my list of odds and ends to try before the end of the year. The massively increased level cap is appealing just for the prospect of seeing exactly how chonky the boars can get now that they scale to my level. The game’s time management system gives you ample opportunity to get the biggest quests done, but not everything can be completed in the 30 days you’re given to save your family.Â  I’m curious to see just how much you actually can get done, both within the time allotted and after everything’s over.

#3572. EA Begs You To Not Delete Madden 27 For GTA 6

We all know what's coming: Grand Theft Auto 6. Whether you're ready for it or not, the most anticipated game of the decade is preparing to launch on November 19, and ahead of its release, EA is begging you to please not ditch footballs for guns.

According to Push Square, EA added a "don't delete" pop-up message to Madden NFL 27. The pop-up says there's an update coming to the football simulator on November 17, just before GTA 6 drops.

"Don't delete," the message reads. "[Encrypted Signal] The target is locked. The crew is assembling for a high-stakes run. Await the signal from our insider on 11/17 ... do not leak this transmission!"

In a November 10 post on Madden NFL 27's official X account, EA said that a throwback Madden 97 update is coming on November 18 with old-school playbooks, 16-bit gameplay, and the All '97 Team. Underneath that post, EA had asked that you stick around a little while longer.

This is in reference to the humongous amount of storage space that Rockstar Games' GTA 6 will take up when it launches. Start clearing out your hard drive now because you need at least 212GB of free space to download GTA 6. In comparison, Madden NFL 27 needs approximately 60GB to install the game.

If you're like me and you still have the base PS5, this means you have approximately 667GB of usable space. Sure, you can fit both GTA 6 and Madden NFL 27 on the same console. However, if you have any other recent releases like The Blood of Dawnwalker (~50GB), Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen (~81GB), Phantom Blade Zero (~135GB), and Valor Mortis (~60GB), then you can see how quickly you'll run out of space--especially since you have to leave a little wiggle room for game updates, too. That's not to mention the games dropping in 2027, such as Final Fantasy VII Revelation, which game director Naoki Hamaguchi said could be around 200GB.

EA has recently gone through a restructuring that saw 400 employees across the company get let go and the legendary studio BioWare get shut down. In the midst of this, the publisher reiterated its commitment to the Madden franchise with a new title currently codenamed Project Gridiron. While filled with potential, we do fear that EA's plan for the series may lean into everything that the company itself does wrong.

Zara Tindall joined in the action at Cheltenham Racecourse on Friday

The royal confidant has four children with her husband Chris: Billy, who studied at Swansea University; Nell, who trained at the Central School of Ballet; a keen skier, Ted; and Mary.

Princess Anne's daughter wrapped up in a warm plaid coat and roll-neck jumper

The Prince of Wales helped to put together the Tusk Conservation Awards at Raffles on Wednesday night and invited Zara to the celebration of conservation, alongside Lady Amelia and Lady Eliza Spencer and the Marchioness of Bath.

Dolly Maud made her debut as lady-in-waiting for the Princess Royal at the 2024 Commonwealth Day Service in March

#3569. GTA 6 Should Help Boost PS5 And Xbox Sales, But Their Astronomical Prices Could Hurt

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, and it's expected to help boost console sales for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. But the uptick in hardware sales might not be as dramatic as you might think--and there is a good reason why.

According to Circana's Mat Piscatella, there will be "probably" be a boost to PS5 and Xbox Series X|S sales when GTA 6 comes out, but the uptick could be muted due to the recent PS5 and Xbox Series X|S price hikes. Piscatella said anyone who is excited for GTA 6 and needs a new console might think twice when they see how astronomically expensive new consoles have become today.

Historical prices

When GTA 5 launched in 2013, the average price paid for a new PS3 was $252 and the Xbox 360 was $232. Adjusted for inflation, that would be $363 for the PS3 today and $334 for the Xbox 360. Those prices are significantly below the average price of a new PS5 ($646) and Xbox Series X|S ($663) today.

"Not a good thing"

Earlier this year, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick, who oversees the company launching GTA 6, said, "The rising cost of hardware is not a good thing." At the same time, Zelnick isn't worried about the impact on GTA 6, in part because he believes the game is so good that people will find a way to pay for a new console.

 "However, a lower price point for hardware would be a good thing because there’d be more hardware in people’s hands," he said. "Probably the most relevant thing is the world continues to move to open systems, and that will continue.”

#3568. People Are Just Straight-Up Illicitly Dumping Games Like Undertale Into Roblox Now

Counter-StrikeDeltaruneParappaRobloxUndertale

Someone has taken the entirety of indie hit Undertale and unceremoniously cloned into Roblox without permission. And Deltarune, all five chapters.

And I don’t mean someone did fan recreations of these games in Roblox with Roblox assets. Nor do I mean they created a unique fan spinoff sort of thing within Roblox using assets from those games. I don’t even mean someone directly ripped all of Deltarune‘s battles and made them playable in Roblox, though someone did do that in August and nearly 200 million people have played it since. I mean someone just straight up took the entire games of Undertale, Deltarune, and others, and stuck them in Roblox.

I first learned about this on Reddit via a post from Personal-News3260 regarding the porting of Deltarune, and it admittedly took a bit of digging to find the port (I’m not going to link any of the games I talk about here for obvious reasons). But I did eventually find it and play it (alongside, apparently, 58,000 other people) and yeah, that’s Deltarune all right. While I obviously was unable (and, frankly, unwilling) to test the game in its entirety, I did play the first half hour or so of Chapter 1 and started all the other chapters, and can confirm that what I saw is undeniably just Deltarune. There are some notable issues, like audio glitches and screen tearing, and one of Susie’s early lines (“Quiet people piss me off”) has been softened to “Quiet people tick me off,” presumably so as not to run afoul of whatever rules still exist on Roblox anymore.

From there, I was able to track down a similar version of Undertale (“created” by the same person), and a community they’re part of where someone has put in what looks to be Parappa the Rappa. I booted both up and from the first few minutes, both definitely look like the actual games.

I also tapped my colleague Zack Zwiezen to look at a Counter-Strike 2 port that I saw being discussed and reported about in multiple places. Zack told me that the game I tracked down and sent him looked, sounded, and played like Counter-Strike 2, but did have different models and a different map, so it wasn’t quite as egregious as the stuff above. From what I can tell, the version of this game shown in the tweet below is the same game I sent him, but it seems to be regularly updated to change models around or restrict access in order to avoid being taken down. At various points, a number of individuals online have shown and reported that it’s largely indistinguishable from Counter-Strike 2.

Counter-Strike fully ported into Roblox…ð³#roblox pic.twitter.com/MKGdS7jH46

When I reached out to Roblox for comment on this practice, I received the following back:

As a platform built by creators, we’re committed to respecting intellectual property rights of independent developers and global brands alike, and every Roblox user agrees to abide by our Terms of Use when they create.

Our Community Standards prohibit content that’s confusingly similar to another Roblox creator’s work, along with repetitive and misleading content, and our moderation systems are built to find and can act on copied games and misleading copycats of Roblox games. For off-platform rights holders, itâs their choice on if and how they would like their IP to be used on Roblox. Rights holders can manage this with tools like our License Manager, which lets them provide and manage licenses at scale, and our Rights Manager, which lets IP holders report content they believe infringes their rights. For those who choose, both Rights and License Manager also allow IP holders to provide reference material that enables Roblox to surface content that matches their IP.

We don’t tolerate IP infringement and act quickly on valid takedown requests, including DMCA notices. Once a game is published to Roblox, it’s held to the same platform-wide IP and clone policies as any other Roblox game, and creators remain responsible for what they choose to publish.

So Roblox’s official policy, of course, is that people are not allowed to just lift other people’s games and drop them into its platform. But they do. And Roblox here is essentially saying it’s not going to sit there and check games to see if they violate policy, until and unless the rights holders themselves get involved and use its tools to report games that violate their own copyrights.

But Roblox is massive! Thousands of games are being updated daily! And none of the games I mentioned above are findable just by searching “Deltarune” or “Parappa” in the search bar. So even though thousands of Roblox users are liable to stumble upon these games by accident or recommendation, because their “creators” have gone to great lengths to use vague names and descriptions in order to hide them from people actively looking for them; they’re deliberately difficult to track down in any specific way. I can imagine a company like Sony might have the resources to assign someone to engage with Roblox’s rights platforms. But I cannot fathom that small indie devs would have that kind of time. I’m sure Toby Fox, for instance, has better things to do than painstakingly search Roblox every day to see if anyone’s dumped his games in there.

With this policy and the advent of AI coding enabling more and more individuals to do such things with little time or effort, Roblox appears to be taking more of a YouTube approach to game uploads. It’s outsourcing the work of whack-a-mole-ing rights violations onto rights holders rather than performing any level of basic screening of a game before it’s allowed to be uploaded.

And that’s by design. In its latest earnings call, Roblox talked extensively about multiple AI-driven initiatives, including one called “The Universal Player.” Essentially, The Universal Player’s goal is to â[enable] the capability to import any existing console, PC, or mobile game onto Roblox.â Per Roblox, what the company wants is for developers who make their games elsewhere to be able to bring them to Roblox and monetize them there, as well as on other platforms. At the moment, this specific feature is not what’s being used to get Deltarune and sundry onto Roblox. “Our tools are still in development, so weâre starting with a select group of partners who hold the necessary rights and have a game that has been released on a major storefront,” wrote Roblox in an email to me. “We have a multi-step process to vet applications, including vetting for ownership. Selected partners must then sign an agreement with us before moving forward.”

But that’s just for now. What’s coming is, again per Roblox, a “new AI-based import technology, which can bring [a developer’s] existing console, PC, and mobile games to Roblox. It uses AI tools built by Roblox to convert a game into a Roblox version.” Assuming that the goal is to eventually roll this out widely, we’re only going to see greater proliferation of vibe-coded renditions of existing games uploaded to Roblox without permission. Nintendo, Steam, PlayStation, and Xbox are already having enough trouble controlling the flood of AI slop, including from “vetted” developers. Roblox’s current tactics do not provide much reassurance that it will do a better job of curation. Given that the “creators” of unauthorized ports like these can and will monetize such endeavors, thereby making money for themselves and for Roblox off of other people’s hard work, I’m not sure it even wants to.

Kotaku also reached out to Valve, Sony, and Toby Fox for comment.

#3566. As Hollywood Battles AI, Pedro Pascal Says Making Behemoth! Filled Him with “a Tremendous Amount of Hope”

Pedro Pascal says that the character he plays in Behemoth!, his first leading film role, is the “closest thing to me that I’ve ever done.” And because of this, “the experience on set felt surreal in a sort of physically tangible way,” Pascal told the audience during a Q&A at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room at LACMA on Saturday.

Directed by Tony Gilroy, Behemoth! tells the story of Alex, a prodigal cellist who returns to Los Angeles and the world of Hollywood film scoring after decades performing symphonic work around the country.

“The mixing of my own life and this person's life, I've lived a very nomadic one. Don't ask me where home is. And so that felt like it was crossing personal lines for me in a way,” he continued during a post-screening discussion about the film, which featured Pascal and writer-director Tony Gilroy, moderated by VF's West Coast Editor John Ross.

But according to Gilroy, their collaboration on the film almost didn't happen, thanks to an alleged missed connection at a Star Wars event.

Tony Gilroy and Pedro Pascal  at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

“We went to a Star Wars convention in Tokyo where we took Andor,” recalled Gilroy. “There was this big Disney dinner so all the Star Wars people are there and [Pascal] was kind of busy and flighty.”

“I had the flu! I flew from London to Tokyo!” Pascal countered.

Gilroy continued: “He seemed like he was so hip that he didn't come to the dinner. I thought, 'Oh he's got such a great thing going on he's going to some better party; he's not going to a boring dinner.'”

As the audience laughed, Pascal was quick to set the record straight: “I cannot believe that you thought that I ditched that dinner. I was doing re-shoots of Fantastic Four!” he said. “They flew me to Tokyo that night and flew me back and I was on a set. [Turns toward the audience] Can you believe this?”

“Oh my God. I'm calling Kathy Kennedy [the President of Lucasfilm] right away,” Gilroy joked.

Luckily, the moviemaking stars (and schedules) aligned and the pair was able to make their personal, moving film with Pascal serving as Gilroy's “exclamation point. He has all the sadness and all the covering that this character needs to have and the nomadic life.”

Pedro Pascal, Tony Gilroy and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Pascal and Gilroy formed a genuine bond and are very comfortable making playful jabs at each other, keeping things light but also expressing their gratitude for being able to make Behemoth! their way, in Los Angeles, where the film and television industry has been struggling to regain a foothold. Despite the challenges, past and present, they are holding out hope for human-made storytelling to foster further human connection.

“People's natural resistance to the robot takeover is clear,” said Gilroy when asked about the rise of AI. “I don't know what's going to happen. I really don't. The music scene out here is the coral reef of what's happened. It's been dying out here for the last 15 years… It's grooving a little bit now. I think people want humans. I don't know what's going to come back, but this is this incredibly humanizing element of movies that's happened. Can it be replaced by AI? Probably, quite shockingly, simply. There's probably an emotional amplitude knob on some f—ing algorithm, but this movie is organic.”

Pedro Pascal and Tony Gilroy  at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Pascal walked away from Behemoth! feeling optimistic. “The experience of shooting this movie definitely injected me with a tremendous amount of hope,” he said. “We weren't making money on this movie. Nobody was. And you had the most expensive people involved in this film because of their talent and their experience. So there was just this purity of love in the work from every single department, and that was incredibly contagious. And it was primarily locations, and so Los Angeles was just constantly revealing itself in all of these magical ways because we were so location-based. I had shot a series in Colombia for three seasons, and I would argue that the primary character of that series, Narcos, was shooting it in the country of Colombia because there was only one way of capturing that energy and that physical story. And LA did that as well. And then it's so tender. I think the story is incredibly tender. Would you ever expect it from this guy [gestures to Gilroy]?”

“Oh my God. What a cold, weird thing to say,” the director joked.

“There are other movies this year that I think in their own way, movies that I've seen this year that I love so much, that fight for humanity and the storytelling,” Pascal continued. “So I think that there is a sort of pushback that could be really, really thrilling as far as [creativity] is concerned, as far as politics is concerned. We want to be human beings and we want to be connected to one another and we want to tell each other's stories and witness each other's stories and we want to look after each other and all that shit. That's my hope.”

Tony Gilroy at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Gilroy had another suggestion: “Blow up the AI centers, man," he joked. “I don't mean to blow them up. I mean blow them up at the voting box. Go and vote and blow them up. Go see the Musk documentary, man. Go see that, watch the whole four hours. I'm pitching my movie [here], but watch that movie.”

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

#3565. WoW: Forever’s Dungeons Have Gotten Yet Another Big Change

World of Warcraft: Forever's dungeons have changed once again, with developer Blizzard's most recent adjustment requiring an emergency hotfix to address players' outcry.

Dungeons, specifically how much experience points players earn from them, have been one of Forever's most debated topics going back to the game's beta. Make them too lucrative, and players will just stay inside dungeons instead of questing out in the world. At the same time, Blizzard doesn't want dungeons to be one-time affairs, with players completing all their quests in a single run and never going back.

Blizzard opened a new front in the dungeon wars on November 13, making a change so that nobody in a dungeon group would receive any experience if enemies were considered "trivial" to to any player in the group. The idea behind this appeared to be an effort to prevent high-level players from running low-level ones through dungeons, in the process curtailing players from selling character "boosting" services to lowbies.

Unfortunately, far too many players playing the game normally were caught in the crossfire. Many of Forever's dungeons have double-digit level ranges, meaning even if a player might find enemies early on in the dungeon trivial, enemies and bosses later on won't be. It also created a scenario where players were leveling up mid-dungeon, only to suddenly find themselves fighting trivial enemies and bricking the experience gains for everyone in the group.

As it turns out, committing to a multi-hour adventure, only to suddenly find nobody is earning experience points and everyone is mad at you because you happened to level up, is not a great social experience. Blizzard was at least quick to admit the change "missed the mark" and made adjustments a day later on November 14.

"With hotfixes that are now live, we've just deployed a further change to this restriction, making it so the XP nullification only kicks in when the high-level player is more than 12 levels above the level of the enemies," Blizzard said in a forum post. 

At least judging from forum comments, that seems to be a more reasonable compromise, even if it still does prevent higher-level players from coming to help their lower-level friends.

It's just the latest chapter in what has become one of the biggest ongoing discussions in the Forever community. During the Forever beta, Blizzard made changes to experience earned from dungeon quests, nerfing them significantly. 

Come launch day, it became apparent Forever's dungeons weren't worth running more than once, as after completing quests, experience earned from kills was extremely low. Blizzard agreed, and issued a change on November 8 to increase the amount of kill experience earned in dungeons by 50%. It was a sizable increase, but is still lower than the experience amount players earned from doing dungeons in WoW Classic.

Forever's launch broke WoW concurrent-player records, and after one week of adventuring through Azeroth once more, classic WoW feels fresh again. Despite the record-breaking launch, Blizzard hasn't released official stats, but fansites have already pieced together the game's most popular class, race, and faction.

#3563. The Head Of GTA 6’s Parent Company Helped Make One Of The Best Christmas Movies Of All Time

One of the most memorable and beloved Christmas movies is 1990's Home Alone, but it almost didn't happen, and the head of GTA 6's parent company played a role in bringing the movie to market.

Strauss Zelnick, the current CEO of Rockstar Games owner Take-Two, was the president and COO of 20th Century Fox at the time--he was among the youngest-ever Hollywood CEOs at the age of 32.

Warner Bros. was originally backing Home Alone and had actually begun production on the movie until budget concerns prompted the studio to pull the plug. "Four days into production, they shut down the picture and canceled it. That never happens," Zelnick told David Rubenstein.

Fox, under the leadership of chairman Joe Roth and Zelnick as president, swooped in and gave the filmmakers--including director Christopher Columbus and writer John Hughes--the money to make Home Alone.

That turned out to be a fantastic investment for Fox, as Home Alone ranked as one of the top five highest-grossing movies of the year in the US. It grossed more than $476 million globally against a $13 million budget, and it picked up two Oscar nominations. Home Alone also helped launch the career of Macaulay Culkin, and his role of Kevin remains his most memorable part.

So why didn't Zelnick keep making movies?

Zelnick was on top of the world as a film executive after Home Alone. However, he said he saw a bright future in the interactive entertainment business, so he left Fox in 1993 to join Crystal Dynamics where he served as president and CEO.

"I left Fox voluntarily, which no one ever does, to move to Silicon Valley, take a 95% pay cut and become the pre-revenue CEO of a little tiny video game company called Crystal Dynamics in 1993," he said in the Rubenstein interview.

After Crystal Dynamics, Zelnick shifted to the music business in the role of CEO as BMG Entertainment from 1994 to 2000. During that time, BMG started a gaming unit, BMG Interactive, which published the original GTA in 1997.

After that, Zelnick and an investor group took over Take-Two, which was in a tough financial spot at the time and was sued by the US government for accounting fraud.

Since the takeover, Take-Two has thrived. Its share price exploded from about $10 in 2007 to more than $220 today, and Take-Two today has a market cap of over $40 billion. The GTA franchise is a juggernaut at Take-Two, but it actually only accounts for 15% of the company's revenue in a non-release quarter. Take-Two today owns and operates a number of big non-GTA franchises, including NBA 2K, Borderlands, Mafia, BioShock, Civilization, and more.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It's reportedly already sold close to 15 million copies and generated nearly $1.5 billion in revenue.

#3562. Newborn Died After Mom Allegedly Beat Him Less Than 1 Hour After He Was Born

A Mississippi woman was arrested after she allegedly beat her newborn son less than one hour after he was born, leading to his death just days later.

Jantelle Sharon Jordan has been charged with capital murder following the death of her son, Jaiden Shane Jordan-Burkes.

The Smith County Sheriff’s Office announced in a press release that deputies and paramedics responded to a home in Polkville, Mississippi, on October 18 after they received a call about a mother giving birth.

Upon their arrival, authorities learned that Jordan, 25, had given birth about an hour earlier while still at the home. The sheriff’s office said that her son was then rushed to the hospital, and he began “experiencing medical complications that initially had an unknown cause.”

Investigators determined that Jaiden had sustained injuries after birth, and he died two days after he was hospitalized.

An autopsy was performed on the boy, which revealed that his cause of death was blunt force trauma. The sheriff’s office added that his manner of death was homicide.

Despite confirming the details of his death, officers did not describe how or why they believe Jordan fatally injured her son.

Following her son’s sudden death, detectives interviewed Jordan on October 24. The woman wasn’t arrested until Friday, November 13. She was taken to the Smith County Jail following her arrest, where she remains in custody.

Authorities said that they are still investigating the case, and they plan to forward their findings to the state attorney’s office for prosecution.

“This is a horrific case for everyone involved in working on this investigation. These are the types of cases that are difficult for anyone to comprehend, especially when they involve the loss of an innocent child,” Sheriff Joel Houston said in a statement.

Jaiden was remembered in an online obituary, in which his family reflected on their short time with him and the future they could have had together.

“Jaiden was born on October 18, 2026, in Smith County, Mississippi, and although his time here was short, he made a lasting impact on the family that loved him so dearly,” the obituary read. “He would have loved racing and riding four wheelers with his father and grandfather.”

It’s not currently clear if Jordan has entered a plea or retained legal counsel following her arrest. The Smith County Sheriff’s Office did not immediately respond to Us’ request for comment regarding updates in the case.

The newest Saturday Night Live episode aired last weekend, with comedian John Mulaney serving as Season 52’s latest host and Phoebe Bridgers performing as the musical guest. Unsurprisingly, the episode began with a cold open centered around recent events, and it centered on the controversy surrounding Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. As part of that segment, Elon Musk was lampooned by the show again and, after he expressed disappointment with the impression, cast member Jeremy Culhane reacted.

SNL’s latest cold open sees the CIA gathering the U.S’ biggest tech magnates for a training session on not exposing secrets to potential operatives. The presiding official (played by Mulaney) speaks to Musk (Jeremy Culhane), Mark Zuckerberg (Andrew Dismukes), Sam Altman (Ben Marshall), Dario Amodei (Jane Wickline) and Peter Thiel (James Austin Johnson). After Mulaney’s character unsuccessfully tries to make his case, Huang (played by returning cast member Bowen Yang) warns his colleagues using his own experience.

Ultimately, the real Elon Musk appeared to be less than impressed with the sketch, in which Mulaney’s character used venn diagrams to explain to the CEOs that a woman wouldn’t truly be interested in them without an ulterior motive. In response, Musk dropped a comment under the sketch on X and included a diagram of his own:

@nbcsnl lol https://t.co/7vw3wS9Jm3November 16, 2026

Throughout the sketch, Culhane’s Musk makes several random statements at the fictional briefing, one of which sees him compare himself to James Bond and another in which he tries to connect with Huang over their leather jackets. It’s because of those random asides that both the CIA official and even Huang use spray bottles on Culhane’s Musk. On X, after someone ranked the performances the actual SpaceX founder shared his take on Culhane’s impression, writing:

I’d give them maybe 5/10 for me. They need to try harder.

This isn’t the first time Musk has taken issue with an impression of himself on Saturday Night Live. Back in late 2024, the tech mogul – who also hosted SNL in 2021 – called out Dana Carvey for his take on him. The following year would also see Musk chastise Mike Meyers’ impression of him as well. The Tesla figurehead is far from the only star to ever take issue with an impression, as Kanye West disliked Chris Redd’s impression of him Also, Ice Cube was dismissive of Kenan Thompson’s take on him.

After this latest Musk impression, Jeremy Culhane took to his Instagram story to share a headline about Musk’s reaction. The Sex Lives of College Girls alum simply added the following caption to his post:

Reading between the lines, Culhane’s response seems to be a bit of trolling on his part. He may not have gone into detail, but it’s easy to get the feeling that he’s not too perturbed by Musk’s reaction to his performance. On the night of the taping, the actor’s performance also generated considerable laughs from the live studio audience. As for whether Musk might feel compelled to issue a response to the comedian’s social media post, that remains to be seen.

What can probably be assumed at this point, however, is that as long as Elon Musk remains in the news, this probably won’t be the last time he’s parodied on the long-running sketch comedy show. Viewers will ultimately just have to wait and see if or how further sketches materialize and for what reason. On that note, check out Saturday Night Live when it airs on the titular night at 11:30 p.m. ET amid the 2026 TV schedule. Episodes are also available to stream with a Peacock subscription.
