#3523. Why Should I Care About GTA 6?

Twas the night before GTA VI, and all through the site, all the writers are prepping for a long, sleepless nightâ

No, sorry, I won’t subject you to that. But here at Kotaku, we’re all abuzz in preparation for several busy days (and weeks, probably months!) of Grand Theft Auto VI coverage. We’ve been chatting with each other a lot about what we’re looking forward to, what we’re hoping for, and what our experiences with the series have been in the past, and it’s come up that I, specifically, have never played a GTA game before. Never touched one, not even for a few minutes.

You can laugh, but I don’t think I’m alone. GTA V has sold nearly 235 million copies, sure, but there are three and a half billion gamers or so in the entire world. A lot of us have never played it, or any GTA game, ever. But maybe, with GTA VI, we are thinking we might want to.

It’s an odd experience, being on the outside for this one, having a vague-ish idea of what GTA is from clips and discussions and posts and reviews, but not actually having taken the controller in my hands and experienced what everyone means when they discuss one of the most popular games of all time. It means that, while I’ve seen the various trailers, I don’t actually have a great grasp on what I’m in for here. You just drive a car around? And steal stuff? Why do people care so much about this? I mean, I know why they care about it, but why do they 5-million-copies-every-three-months, take-a-week-off-from-their-job, dump-hundreds-of-dollars-on-a-console, ignore-significant-other-for-days care about this?

I tapped Kotaku‘s two foremost GTA experts, Zack and Carolyn, to explain the phenomenon to me. I hope that those of you out there (there are dozens of us!) who are in the same highly stealable vehicle as me on this one will get something out of their insight!

Rebekah Valentine: What were both of your very first experiences with GTA? How did you come into the series?

Zack Zwiezen: A friend brought over his copy of GTA III on PS2 and booted it up for me and it blew my mind. I was 10? Around that age. I remember walking around that world, getting into a car, driving the streets, and just never hitting a level-end screen or mission. I could just explore this big city forever. It was unlike anything I had played before. I ended up buying the game myself from that kid later using lunch money I saved up, and played many, many hours of GTA III. I’ve been a fan of the franchise ever since.

Carolyn Petit: I had seen the first few top-down games here and there but only ever in passing; they didnât really catch my interest. It wasnât until Jeff Gerstmann’s review for Grand Theft Auto IIIÂ appeared on GameSpot, the one gaming site I read religiously in those days, that I really sat up and took notice as it sounded like something special. I went out and bought the game immediately, and as soon as I fired it up and experienced that opening scene in which youâre busted out of an armored police truck and have to make your getaway through a grungy, modern American city, I knew I was seeing games change forever, in much the same way I had when I first saw Mario run to the right in Super Mario Bros. and people putting quarters on the marquee of a Street Fighter 2 cabinet at my local 7-Eleven.

Zack: I’ve gone back over the years and played the first games, the top down ones. And they’re fun, but playing them now it’s hard to imagine that those games would lead to the biggest video game series in the world.

Carolyn: Right! In so many ways the whole existence of GTA as this massive cultural juggernaut feels like a fluke. Those early games struck me as an edgy curiosity, games that drew attention for âpushing the limitsâ because they let you play as a criminal and kill civilians but not actually particularly good or interesting as games.

Rebekah: I grew up Catholic, and I always heard about GTA from parents and teachers as this vice-ridden thing. It was the subject of a lot of moral panic, for years! I obviously have a different impression of it now (and donât really care about playing a game about sin anyway), but I have to admit that that being my worldview for so long really helped ensure I didnât know anything else, really, about the game. Like, I think in my head for years it was just a game in which you drove around doing murders and robberies, gambling, and seducing women. Which, maybe thatâs accurate!

Nowadays, having matured beyond that perspective, I guess I assumed the older games had a lot more going on in them. Butâ¦maybe they didnât? When did these games become, to use Carolynâs words, âgood and interestingâ, do you think?

Carolyn: When GTA III came along, I admit it, I couldnât get enough. And it wasnât because I loved its crime narrative. That narrative is functional, but itâs not great or anything. What defined my experience of GTA III were all the sort of emergent experiences I had with it that created these moments that were really kind of beautiful. I remember driving along in the game and the rain started to fall while the song âFade Awayâ was playing on the radio, and it just felt like this incredible cinematic moment, this glimpse of beauty in the midst of urban decay. Itâs moments like that which have really stayed with me from that first game (well, third but you know what I mean), though of course it was also just really fun to push the limits of what was possible, to wreak havoc, try to steal a tank or whatever. It was a game that encouraged play within a context and with systems that no game Iâd played before had.

Zack: There are really three distinct eras of GTA. It has always been open world, letting you do whatever, which is still the big appeal of these games. But in the top-down era, things were more cartoonish and wacky. The 3D era, when the games made the leap to PS2, is when they start to mature a bit. Still, GTA III, for all the great vibes, is at times a very goofy game that feels like it’s populated entirely by people pretending to be mobsters, cops, and criminals.

GTA IV, the start of the âHD Era,â is really when GTA evolved into what is today. Thatâs when the games, starting with Nikoâs journey in GTA IV, got more serious and tried to tell more mature stories about real people. I don’t think GTA V nailed that as well as GTA IV, but if you’re asking when they became more than just âdriving and shooting cops,â thatâs the timeline, I think.

But for me, not sure how Carolyn feels, the reason I keep coming back to GTA and get excited for a new one isnât to see what story Rockstar is going to tell next. Instead, Iâm here for the world. Getting to live in that virtual space and explore it. Thatâs the real appeal. And a big reason is because Rockstar are far and away the best at making detailed, sprawling open worlds that feel alive.

Carolyn: Oh, absolutely. To be clear, Iâve really liked some aspects of some GTA stories. I think San Andreas has some interesting themes about police corruption and tries to engage with the pressure cooker that Los Angeles was in the â90s. Iâm not saying it handles that wholly successfully or says anything particularly insightful, but it was novel at the time just to see a game make the effort. And there are individual characters and moments in that game that are quite well-written, little moments of beauty amid the silliness and carnage. And yeah, GTA IV remains for now my favorite narrative in the series. Niko had some real shit going on, and his focus on revenge can play out in ways that I found affecting. But yes, what really elevates the GTA games in my view has always been their worlds. They just exude a kind of environmental authenticity that far surpasses what most other games offer. Really, little has changed for me since GTA IIIÂ in terms of what become my most memorable moments from any GTA game. Those moments usually involve the right song on the radio at the right time when Iâm in the right place to just create an immaculate vibe, maybe something about the sunset hitting the ocean just so or whatever it is, in a way that I just find breathtaking.

Rebekah: Maybe the answer to this is just reiterating what you both just said, but like, okay, I get why these games are special, but why are they this special? Why is GTA V selling five million copies every three months? Why is the entire internet batshit crazy over GTA VI? Like I get it, theyâre very technically impressive, the freedom is cool, the online has a lot going on, and so forth. But what is it that elevates these games so dang far above every other game in the level of attention and frenzy theyâre getting? Is it just what youâre describing here, that itâs that good? #3522. GTA 6’s Lucia Actor Revealed, And It’s The Person Everyone Already Guessed

The actor playing Lucia in Grand Theft Auto 6 has been revealed, and it's Manni L. Perez, the person everyone expected it to be for a long time now. In fact, fans discovered that Perez was Lucia all the way back in 2023.

The news didn't come from Rockstar Games or the actor herself, but instead via The Game Awards. That's because Perez was nominated for Best Performance. GTA 6, meanwhile, was nominated for overall Game of the Year this year, and that's sorta awkward because reviews for the game aren't live yet.

Perez was nominated for Best Performance alongside Patrick Gibson (007 First Light), Angela Sant'Albano (Resident Evil Requiem), Liam McIntyre (Marvel's Wolverine), and Rahul Kohli (Saros). The actor playing Jason in GTA 6 remains a mystery, but people widely believe it's Dylan Rourke.

GTA 6 leads the way this year at The Game Awards with eight nominations. These include:

  • Game of the Year
  • Best Game DIrection
  • Best Narrative
  • Best Art Direction
  • Best Score and Music
  • Best Audio Design
  • Best Performance (Manni L. Perez)
  • Best Action/Adventure Game

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with a PC release reportedly on tap for early 2027.

In addition to Perez as Lucia and someone else as Jason, we've learned that veteran actor Stephen Root will play Brian Heder. People believe Saturday Night Live actor Bobby Moynihan is playing Cal Hampton, but this is not confirmed yet. For more, check out all the GTA 6 confirmed and rumored actors.

#3521. Brad Pitt and GF Ines de Ramon Hold Hands During Rare Red Carpet Appearance

Brad Pitt and his girlfriend, Ines de Ramon, couldn’t contain their smiles while walking the red carpet.

The couple stepped out on Monday, November 16, to attend the premiere of Netflix’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth in Los Angeles, which Pitt, 62, stars in as the titular character. Pitt and de Ramon, 33, held hands on their date night.

For the event, Pitt opted for a navy sweater and pants with a double-breasted coat and accessorized with a pair of sunglasses. De Ramon, for her part, stunned in a cream dress with cutouts at the waist and a plunging neckline. She styled her hair down in loose curls as she beamed with pride at the world premiere.

Pitt and de Ramon have been linked since 2022 when they were first spotted joining friends Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber at a Bono concert at the Orpheum Theatre in Los Angeles. Two years later, Pitt and de Ramon debuted their romance at the British Grand Prix. Pitt, for his part, has denied that the 2024 appearance was part of a planned promotional event for his 2025 film F1.

“No, dude, it’s not that calculated,” he recalled to GQ in a May 2025 profile. “If you’re living … oh, my God, how exhausting would that be? If you’re living with making those kinds of calculations? No, life just evolves. Relationships evolve.”

The pair have since given glimpses of their relationship, with Pitt opening up about how he and de Ramon enjoyed a date-night at Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s star-studded wedding in July.

“You mean, the wedding of the century? Let me tell you, that was such an amazing night,” Pitt told Entertainment Tonight in September when asked about the phone-free event. “I think we were there [for] 10 hours, maybe 12.”

Pitt and de Ramon matched in coordinating black formalwear at the event, which was held at New York City’s Madison Square Garden.

“It was so thoughtful and well-planned and really moving and great fun,” Pitt gushed. “But it was big, and at one point, I lost her in the melee on the dance floor.”

But the pair reunited quickly. “Not long. There’s always someone to go, ‘That way,’” he said, pretending to point in opposite directions.

Prior to his relationship with de Ramon, Pitt was previously married to Jennifer Aniston from 2000 to 2005 and later to Angelina Jolie, with whom he shares six children, from 2014 to 2019.

#3520. GTA 6 Leads TGA Nominations, And Reviews Aren’t Even Live Yet

The Keighleys, or more formally, The Game Awards, are right around the corner. Ahead of its December 10 air date, host Geoff Keighley announced the nominees for the myriad categories, including Game of the Year. Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto 6 made the cut, but in an unusual circumstance, it did so before any reviews of the game have been published.

Before anyone has read any official take on GTA 6, Rockstar Games' action-adventure game has eight nominations, making it the most-nominated game at this year's The Game Awards.

On top of being spotlighted for Game of the Year, the game also has nominations for Best Art Direction, Best Audio Design, Best Game Direction, Best Action/Adventure, Best Narrative, Best Performance (for Manni L. Perez's portrayal of Lucia), and Best Score, bringing the crime sim's total nominations to eight.

We already knew GTA 6 would be eligible for this year's ceremony. After all, per the TGA FAQ, the cutoff date for eligibility is November 20, one day after the game comes out. With a "jury of over 100 global media and influencer outlets" selecting the nominees, and many of these folks likely having plenty of hands-on time with Rockstar Games' latest release, it isn't much of a shocker to see GTA 6 at the top spot. Still, it is a little awkward that it has so many nominations before its release that may reveal what to expect from the critical reception..

Maybe it shouldn't be too surprising or weird, though. After all, the game isn't officially out yet, and it's already sold approximately 16 million copies and generated nearly $2 billion in revenue. Maybe that expensive sick day caused by the GTA Flu won't be so expensive.

#3518. What Does It Take For World Of Warcraft To Be Nominated At The Game Awards?

The nominees for 2026's The Game Awards have been revealed, and just like every year before it, there is a glaring omission in the Best Ongoing Game Category: World of Warcraft.

This year's nominees are Arc Raiders, Fortnite, No Man's Sky, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, and Final Fantasy 14 Online. Of particular note is Square Enix's MMORPG, which has been nominated in the category every year since 2021. Developer Blizzard's MMO, on the other hand, is nowhere to be seen. 

WoW is among the most popular live-service games in industry history and has been for 22 years. Blizzard releases new expansions for its MMORPG every other year like clockwork and has done so for over two decades. It reintroduced the old-school version of the MMO, WoW Classic, in 2019 to huge acclaim from the game's passionate community.

In the years that followed, it continued to add new expansions to the modern version of WoW, adding highly requested features like account-wide unlocks and new endgame solo content. For WoW Classic, it re-released past expansions, added official servers and support for a permadeath mode popular among the game's community, and ran experimental seasons that added new content to the classic version of the game. Taken all together, the various versions of WoW have millions of players.

Earlier this year, Blizzard released Midnight, the latest expansion for modern WoW that added player housing to the MMO for the first time. A few weeks ago, it released WoW: Forever, the third major version of the MMO. Built on the bones of WoW Classic, Forever is intended to be an ongoing game that will add new content and changes to the old-school version of WoW, existing alongside the modern game. Forever was the biggest launch in WoW history in terms of concurrent players, Blizzard said.

Yet, since 2017, WoW has never even been nominated in Best Ongoing Game, a category that serves to put a spotlight on titles that continue to receive new content and evolve the experience over time--something Blizzard wrote the book on with WoW.

WoW being omitted this year in particular is more baffling than any time before, as Blizzard not only released a brand-new expansion, but also an entirely new version of the game that players have dreamed about for years. On the other hand, Final Fantasy 14's new expansion, Evercold, doesn't release until 2027, even if the game has received significant content updates over the course of the year. 

Even other Blizzard games have been nominated in this category multiple times over the years. Overwatch won Best Ongoing Game in 2017 and was nominated again in 2018. Diablo 4 earned a nomination in 2024 with the release of its first expansion, Vessel of Hatred. 

Meanwhile, it seems like nothing WoW does is enough to warrant attention. There is, of course, a simple answer to why this seems to be the case--nobody, or at least very few, on the The Game Awards voting jury plays, or keeps up to date, with WoW.

That's a shame, because if there was any year where WoW deserved to be nominated, it's this year. Forever is the culmination of an entire community's dream of having an ongoing, new version of classic WoW, and Midnight continues the philosophy of player-friendly changes first added in 2024's The War Within expansion. There are now more ways to play WoW than ever before, each receiving unprecedented support and updates. In fact, players in the modern version of WoW have been complaining that there's perhaps too much to do and that content updates are maybe too frequent. 

This is all to say that it feels like WoW deserves just a little recognition. It's been running for over two decades at this point, and in that time has in many ways defined what an "ongoing game" is and can be. 2026 has been a banner year for WoW, and its future is looking brighter than ever. It deserved a moment in the spotlight. Maybe next year (though I wouldn't bet on it).

#3516. Man Killed Ex-GF and New BF in Murder-Suicide Following History of Abuse

A heartbroken mother shared details about her daughter’s abusive relationship with her ex-boyfriend after police said he allegedly killed her and her new boyfriend in a horrific murder-suicide.

Verchna Philippe and her boyfriend, Darnell McLean, were fatally shot by her ex Scloiwen Jean-Baptiste while they were driving in Miami Gardens in the early hours of Sunday, November 15. Investigators said that after Jean-Baptiste, 27, pulled up to their vehicle in an Uber, he shot Philippe, 25, and she crashed into a fence. McLean, 25, then tried to run away, but Jean-Baptiste chased him and shot him.

Jean-Baptiste returned to the car and shot Philippe a second time before he died by suicide.

McLean and Jean-Baptiste died at the scene, while Philippe was taken to Aventura Hospital for treatment before she died from her injuries.

“She was my right hand, my everything,” Philippe’s mother, Nadege Jean Pierre, told NBC Miami of her late daughter.

Jean Pierre explained that she had waited all night for her daughter to come home, and she didn’t learn what happened until detectives reported to her home the next morning.

“I asked, ‘Is she dead? What happened to my daughter? Where is Verchna?'” she recalled.

Jean Pierre went on to reflect on her daughter’s relationship with Jean-Baptiste, whom police said had a criminal history that dated back to 2015.

“He is a psychopath; he is a maniac,” Jean Pierre said, claiming that Jean-Baptiste has threatened Philippe in the past. “He was obsessed with my daughter.”

Police said that he threatened to kill her in 2024 and also stabbed her during a 2025 incident, according to the outlet.

Jean Pierre said that the stabbing incident happened when Philippe was getting into an Uber and Jean-Baptiste jumped in behind her. “She tried to take the knife from him, but he refused, and he stabbed my daughter,” she said.

McLean’s mother, who asked to not be publicly named, also opened up about the tragedy while speaking to the outlet. “I don’t have words to say how deep it hurts,” she said. “You took my life when you took my son’s life.”

#3515. Does Jesus Christ Exist In World Of Warcraft?

When you die in World of Warcraft, regardless of whether you’re playing Classic or retail or Forever or whatever (as long as you’re not playing hardcore mode), the same thing happens every time.

First, you get a little pop-up window that invites you to get a “recap” of how you died and will tell you what moves did damage to you and how much. That same window also has a “Release Spirit” option which you’ll have to press eventually if you want to keep playing.

When you hit “Release Spirit,” you’re transported to the nearest Graveyard, which may or may not be located a whole-ass ten-minute walk from where you died. Your screen will appear in black and white with a ghostly filter. Your character will not be able to interact with anything, use items, speak, or really do much of anything except move. And move you must, back to your corpse, at which point you can return to your body and continue with whatever you were doing before. Alternatively, you can resurrect yourself at the graveyard, but doing so will break your equipment and give you a horrible ten-minute debuff, so it’s not recommended except in dire situations.

But let’s go back to those moments when you’re running back to your dead body and everything is all ghostly. There’s some music playing while you’re doing that. It’s the same, again, in every version of WoW, and always has been. This is it:

All right, now what in the gosh darn heck is going on here?

Listen to that music. Hear those vocals? Know what they’re singing? It’s not some made-up video game language, people! That there isÂ Latin, the traditional language of the Roman Catholic Church, and those voices are singing “Agnus Dei” over and over, loud and clear. Agnus Dei, for those who did not grow up participating in the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass, means “Lamb of God.” It’s referring toÂ Jesus Christ, specifically as he’s referred to by John the Baptist in the Bible book of John (not the Baptist).

Has anyone else ever thought this was super goofy? Just me? Very, very few songs in World of Warcraft have lyrics. Most of the background music is purely instrumental, intended to be thematic and ambient to your journey. There are a few pieces with vocals, but almost every time they come up, they’re either a sort of non-descript chorus of Ahhhs and Ohhhs, or they’re sung in an actual language invented for this fictional video game. See one of my absolute faves, “Nightsong” from the Cataclysm expansion. It’s in elf language:

So I return to: Why is there a single song in World of Warcraft, a song that’s been in the game since its inception and which every single player has to listen to repeatedly if they have the music on in every incarnation of the game, in which a chorus of voices are singing the Agnus Dei? What could this possibly be meant to imply? Are the words “Agnus Dei” meaningful in some way to the people of Azeroth? Is there some sort of Christian afterlife attached to this world? I feel like that can’t be right given everything we went through in Shadowlands, but I think the takeaway from that expansion is that there are many different afterlives, including many we don’t see. Could that mean that a heaven with Jesus in it exists somewhere, and our WoW characters are destined for it when we die for real?

Did Jesus die for the sins of the people of Azeroth, too? Is he the Lamb of God who takes away the sins of all the worlds, including Azeroth? Because good Lord, there’s a lot of sinning going on down there. Lots of violence, murder, and such. Whatever the Warlock Succubus pet is doing certainly isn’t permitted by the Ten Commandments. Azerothians almost assuredly need whatever salvation they can get.

I do not want to simply believe that the answer is “Someone thought it sounded cool once.” I refuse, and am instead demanding accountability from Blizzard, Jason Hayes, Glenn Stafford, Derek Duke, and Tracy W. Bush. I would also be willing to hear from any theologians who have opinions on this. My email inbox is open and waiting to hear your explanation. In the meantime, I am dead again thanks to the assholes over in Dun Garok who don’t want to share Humbert’s Sword with me, so I will be listening to “Agnus Dei” on loop for the next several minutes and reminding myself of the life, death, and resurrection of Christ.

#3514. This GTA 6-Inspired Keycap Set Will Make The Wait For A PC Version Slightly Easier

Grand Theft Auto 6 is now just a couple of hours away in some parts of the world. That is, if you're planning to play on either Xbox or PlayStation. The wait for a PC version is still ongoing, with Rockstar yet to indicate when it plans to release that port. In the meantime, however, you can start ensuring that your setup is at least ready for when it arrives.

High-end keycap manufacturer GMK has revealed a new set that is clearly inspired by GTA 6 and Vice City, without explicitly mentioning either. The new set, named Neon Vice, features black keycaps with an array of colored alphas and numerical keys, all drawing from the pink, orange, and purple colors of Rockstar's impending sequel. Novelty keycaps include images of speedboats across choppy water, palm trees, and alligators, and the Vice City skyline.

Like most GMK sets, the keycaps are constructed from double-shot ABS plastic, which should ensure fantastic legibility with use over time. What isn't normal is the price, however. GMK keycap sets are priced at a premium, and Neon Vice is no exception. Expect to pay $170 for the base kit, and an additional $45 if you want the novelty keys on top of that. Preorders open for the kit today across multiple vendors around the world.

That's a lot more than the game itself, so if you haven't been bitten by the custom keyboard bug, it's probably best to just continue waiting. Thankfully the gap between console and PC versions for GTA 6 might not be as large as previous Rockstar titles, with a report suggesting that it might arrive in early 2027. If you are playing on console you can pre-load the game right now ahead of its launch, which will start for lucky players in New Zealand very soon.

Robert Pattinson has had a pretty ridiculous year. Between The Drama, Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, and the upcoming Dune: Part Three on the 2026 movie schedule, he's been keeping busy. Now, as if playing the Dark Knight wasn't enough, he's officially been cast as the next James Bond. Naturally, the announcement has generated plenty of reactions, but I wasn't expecting Jon Stewart to have one of the funniest takes I've heard so far.

During Monday night's episode of The Daily Show, Stewart addressed the Bond casting while discussing a string of technological disasters and travel disruptions that had made headlines over the weekend. Somehow, he wove them all into an increasingly ridiculous story about how he was supposed to audition for 007. The lengths he went to before revealing that the Twilight franchise breakout star had beaten him to the role had me laughing out loud. Stewart joked:

I was supposed to fly out to a gig. An audition, actually. Kind of a big one. And obviously, delays at the airport. No big deal. I just thought, well, I'll just go by my preferred travel method, Mississippi riverboat.

When your flight gets canceled, logic dictates that the next step is to hop aboard a riverboat. Obviously. Unfortunately for Stewart, his backup transportation wasn't particularly reliable either, and things only got worse when he tried to contact the people running the audition. He continued the bit:

Unfortunately, we also ran into a bit of a... well, it ran into us, but... so I just thought, well, I'll let the production know I was going to be late by sending them an email from my beloved Microsoft Outlook account. And then the... uh... which... it would have been fine, as long as I could still electronically withdraw the money to rent a car, which... long story short, they ended up giving the role to [BLEEP] Robert Pattinson.

I was already laughing at the idea of Stewart missing out on a big role because his riverboat ran into trouble and Microsoft Outlook wasn't cooperating. But he saved his best complaint for last, taking issue with the fact that Pattinson already has another pretty famous character on his résumé. Raising his fist in mock frustration, the longtime late-night host shouted:

Pattinson! You already got Batman. Enough's enough!

I mean, he's got a point. How many iconic characters does one guy need? Here's an actor who has already played Edward Cullen in the Twilight movies, Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter, and Bruce Wayne in The Batman. Now he's adding 007 to the résumé. At this rate, I half expect someone to announce him as the next Superman. Hey, with James Gunn’s recent outing anything is possible.

Of course, Stewart was having fun with the news, and I don't think anybody seriously believes Pattinson should be disqualified from playing Bond because he's already Batman. But I do think it's funny that the actor is becoming the face of another enormous franchise while he's still working on The Batman: Part II.

Pattinson's casting as James Bond was officially announced Monday, following years of speculation about who would replace Daniel Craig. The upcoming 26th Bond movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, who also worked with the Die My Darling actor on Dune: Part Three. While plenty of actors were rumored to be in contention, Pattinson ultimately landed the role. The announcement has already generated strong reactions from fans, which is hardly surprising given how attached people are to the franchise.

Personally, I'm curious to see what he brings to Bond. He's spent years choosing interesting projects and taking roles that don't always seem like the obvious next step for somebody who became famous playing a sparkly vampire. His Batman was a particularly interesting take on Bruce Wayne, and I wouldn't be surprised if he approached 007 with the same willingness to make the character his own. Although now I also kind of want to hear him deliver the famous Bond introduction in his Batman voice.

Robert Pattinson's first James Bond movie doesn't have a release date yet, although production is expected to begin sometime in 2027. Meanwhile, The Batman: Part II is currently scheduled for February 2028.

Personally, I think it would be hilarious if Pattinson's next role was playing Jon Stewart in a biopic. Stranger things have happened in Hollywood, and at this point, Stewart might want to keep an eye on those casting announcements.

In the meantime, you can catch Stewart hosting The Daily Show Mondays at 11 p.m. ET on Comedy Central, with new episodes available to stream the following morning with a Paramount+ subscription.

#3512. These Are Some Of The Biggest Snubs At The Game Awards 2026

The nominees for The Game Awards have been announced. Some of the biggest games--and those that aren't out yet--make appearances on the list, including Grand Theft Auto 6 and Phantom Blade Zero, but some of the games could've--and maybe should've--been nominated in multiple categories. So, let's go over some of the biggest snubs at this year's TGAs.

Let's start with the big one: Game of the Year. You've got six games nominated here: 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Grand Theft Auto 6, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. All of them are fabulous and well-deserved, but a couple of games are missing: House House's co-op adventure Big Walk and Rebel Wolves' vampire RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker. They appear elsewhere, sure, but I think they deserve GOTY contention, as well.

Let's move onto Best Performance. You've got some stellar voice work here: Angela Sant’Albano as Grace Ashcroft in Resident Evil Requiem, Liam McIntyre as James "Logan" Howlett in Marvel's Wolverine, Manni L. Perez as Lucia Caminos in GTA 6, Patrick Gibson as James Bond in 007 First Light, and Rahul Kohli as Arjun Devraj in Saros. Not taking anything away from these incredible voice talents, but Nick Apostolides as Leon Kennedy in Resident Evil Requiem, Sean Durrie as Dylan Faden in Control Resonant, and Will de Renzy-Martin as Coen in The Blood of Dawnwalker deserve some recognition, too.

Marathon could've easily been nominated for Best Art Direction and Best Action Game. Overwatch and WoW/WoW: Forever would've made sense in the Best Ongoing Game category. Denshattack's soundtrack is too good not to be nominated for Best Score and Music. And Castlevania: Belmont's Curse could slot into a number of categories, including Best Action/Adventure Game, Best Art Direction, and Best Narrative.

There are probably many others that have come out this year that maybe could--and maybe should--have been nominated but weren't for one reason or another. (Note: GameSpot is among the publications that contribute to the nomination process.)

Regardless, we won't have to wait too long to learn what games win what categories, as The Game Awards will air live on December 10 at 4:30 PM PT / 7:30 PM ET.

#3511. Robert Pattinson Is the New James Bond

It looks like Robert Pattinson is trading in his Batmobile for an Aston Martin. After a highly scrutinized and lengthy audition process involving some of Hollywood’s most sought-after leading men, it was the Batman star who emerged at the eleventh hour to nab the role of MI6 agent James Bond.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” said Pattinson in a statement. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

Created by Ian Fleming for his 1953 novel Casino Royale, James Bond, the British intelligence officer who lends his immense talents to MI6, is one of the most recognizable characters in the modern world. Figuring prominently in 12 of Fleming’s novels and two collections of short stories, Bond is both tall, dark, and handsome and calm, cool, and collected—the platonic ideal of a world-class spy. Bond leapt from page to screen in 1962 with the Eon-produced Dr. No, spawning one of the biggest media franchises in history. Since its inception, the 27 Bond films have grossed more than $7 billion dollars worldwide.

Pattinson follows in the suave footsteps of Daniel Craig, who played James Bond for five films, from 2006’s Casino Royale until 2021’s No Time to Die where (spoiler alert) Craig’s 007 dies while protecting the world from a global terrorist organization. Around No Time to Die, there was another shake up in Bond ownership when Amazon acquired Bond’s parent studio, MGM, in an $8.5 billion deal. Barbara Broccoli—whose father, Eon founder Albert R. “Cubby” Broccoli, produced the first Bond film—and her half brother, Michael G. Wilson, held the rights to the franchise for almost 30 years, and pledged to work with Amazon. However, in February 2025, Broccoli and Wilson announced that they’d be stepping back from the franchise and ceding complete creative control to Amazon MGM. At the Oscars a month later, the Broccoli family was honored with a bizarre musical tribute to James Bond, starring Margaret Qualley, Doja Cat, and Lisa, unofficially ushering in a new era in the Bond Cinematic Universe.

Although a new era of Bond loomed, Amazon MGM had one major problem: They needed a new Bond. Ahead of No Time to Die, Craig had announced that he was stepping away from the franchise, leaving the producers with a 007-sized hole to fill. Before she stepped away, Broccoli insinuated that this new era of Bond was looking for a younger actor, in their 30s, to take over the reins from Craig, who was 51 when he retired from MI6.

Technically, they landed on someone slightly outside their preferred age range; Pattinson is 40 years old. Just don’t tell him that. During Vanity Fair’s lie detector test with Jennifer Lawrence while promoting their film Die My Love, Pattinson insisted he was from a different generation. I am Gen Z,” he said to Lawrence. “I am.” Hey, you’re only as old as you feel. In the same video, Pattinson said he “likes taking jobs of younger actors,” which he managed to do with his Bond casting. Good for Pattinson.

Almost every leading man in Hollywood’s name came up as a potential predecessor to Craig—except for Pattinson, who the masses assumed was out of contention due to the fact that he locked into playing another beloved fictional character with massive IP: Batman. Pattinson’s take on the caped crusader in Matt Reeve’s The Batman (2022) was a major success, but several production delays on The Batman Part II, and a shakeup at Batman’s studio, DC—last week, it was announced that the co-CEOs of DC Productions, James Gunn and Peter Safran, were ousted from the studio—meant that there might be time in Pattinson’s schedule for some sexy espionage.

Still, it was far from a done deal that Pattinson would land 007. In recent years, some fans have advocated for a twist on the classic Bond formula. Lashana Lynch made history as Nomi, the first Black person to ever to hold the 007 moniker, in No Time to Die. But Nomi is not James Bond. There was a seemingly endless period when the world was convinced that Idris Elba—arguably the most tall, dark, and handsome man to ever exist—would take on the mantle at some point, but it wasn’t meant to be. Now, at 53, Elba has seemingly aged out of the role. (For the record, Elba thought the next Bond should be a woman.) Elba wasn’t the only name bandied about in recent years. It was reported in 2024 that Aaron Taylor-Johnson was close to signing a contract to take over the role, but those reports were never confirmed.

Although a favorite at the beginning, Jacob Elordi reportedly didn’t screen test for the role. Riz Ahmed made an Emmy-nominated television show, Bait, inspired by the idea of a British Pakistani actor getting cast as Bond. Other actors rumored to be in the mix over the course of the process include, but are not limited to, Tom Francis, Harris Dickinson, and, apparently, Harry Styles. At the end of the day, five actors reportedly screen-tested for the role: Slow Horse’s Jack Lowden, One Night Only’s Callum Turner, Disclosure Day’s Josh O’Connor, Superman’s Nicholas Hoult, and Pattison. Hoult and Pattinson were the last names to emerge as contenders for the role, implying that the powers that be at Amazon MGM may not have been happy with the three options presented and sent a hail mary. When Puck reported that Pattinson was able to negotiate a three-picture deal rather than a four-picture deal despite commanding a much higher salary than the other options, it looked like the writing was on the wall that Pattinson would be the next Bond.

It also helps that Pattinson is having a career high at the moment, having starred in a handful of the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful films of 2026. He began the year by turning his controversial A24 comedy The Drama with Zendaya into a box-office success, generating $134 million worldwide on a reported budget of about $28 million. He then followed that up with a deliciously sniveling turn in Christopher Nolan’s epic The Odyssey, an Oscar front-runner that earned $1.8 billion at the box office. Then there’s Primetime, the Lance Oppenheim drama starring Pattinson as To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen. (Yes, in a way, Chris Hansen is now one degree from being James Bond. Let that sink in). Primetime hit big with $62 million globally on an $14.5 million budget, and is earning Pattinson leading-actor buzz. On top of it all, he’s still got Dune: Part Three with Denis Villeneuve coming down the pipeline in December.

Ultimately, the Twilight star was handpicked by the powers that be at Amazon MGM, including producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman and director Denis Villeneuve, who is helming the next iteration of the series based on a script from screenwriter Steven Knight, with Tanya Lapointe executive producing. Given the fact that Pattinson is starring in Villeneuve’s highly-anticipated Dune: Part Three, it might not be that much of a surprise that the director chose Pattinson as his next Bond. “Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey,” said Villeneuve in a statement. “We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.”

Pattinson enters a long lineage of spectacularly suave spies—some who lasted longer than others in Bond’s impeccably tailored suits. The first-ever James Bond was, of course, Sean Connery, who went on to star in six Bond films, including From Russia With Love (1963), Goldfinger (1964), and Diamonds Are Forever (1971). Connery was followed by George Lazenby, who starred in a single Bond film, On Her Majesty’s Secret Service (1969), before passing the reins back to Connery. The third Bond was Roger Moore, who took over for 1973’s Live and Let Die, and appeared in a total of seven Bond films, most notably The Spy Who Loved Me (1977) and Octopussy (1983).

After Moore came Timothy Dalton, who became 007 with 1987’s The Living Daylights, then threw in the towel after 1989’s License to Kill. Millennials will fondly remember the next Bond: Pierce Brosnan, who starred as the sexy spy in four films from 1995’s GoldenEye to 2002’s Die Another Day, until Craig took over in 2006.

Will Pattison’s Bond be more debonair like Brosnan, who told VF he was “eagerly” awaiting the Bond casting news, or brooding like Craig? Will he be remembered as a rightful heir to Connery’s throne, or will his Bond feel closer to Austin Powers in The Spy Who Shagged Me? In any case, let’s hope Pattinson prefers his martinis shaken not stirred. He’s going to be drinking a lot of them for the foreseeable future.

#3510. 007 First Light Might Be The End Of The Line For James Bond’s Favorite Watch

After months of searching and numerous potential frontrunners, Robert Pattinson has been cast as the next James Bond. It's lead to some questions about whether he's too famous or too old for the role, whether or not he looks like Bond, and just how different his portrayal might be to those that came before him. For some others, however, the questions is far more direct: What watch is he going to wear?

James Bond has long had recognizable brand associations, but one that has endured has been the partnership with luxury watch maker Omega. Bond was first seen wearing an Omega in 1995's GoldenEye, and was mostly recently seen sporting the latest iteration of the Seamaster Diver 300m in this year's 007 First Light. Although not a new film in the series, First Light still featured its own unique take on the Seamaster, the first ever created for a videogame, with Omega adding it to its bursting 007 collection that it makes available for purchase.

So given that it's been three decades, why could First Light be the last iteration of James Bond wearing an Omega? Simply put, Robert Pattinson doesn't wear one, and has very recently become a brand ambassador for one of Omega's Swiss competitors, Jaeger-LeCoultre. There's no confirmation that Pattinson's obligations will directly influence a brand deal between Omega and new Bond owners Amazon, but the omission of any watch at all in the announcement trailer sure has cause some speculation.

Daniel Craig, during his tenure as Bond, was Omega's chief ambassador, often wearing unreleased models to drum up interest for imminent releases. That might not be the case with Pattinson, which could suggest a change for what timepiece his Bond decides to switch to.

If Bond were to jump from Omega to JLC, it would be somewhat fitting. The watch maker manufactures some extremely elegant pieces with a rich history associated with each line. But none makes as much sense as the rectangular Reverso. The watch is distinct in its design, allowing the wearer to rotate the face and flip it 180 degrees, with a variety of designs on the back. Initially created for polo players to protect their prized wristwatches, you can clearly see a lot of potential for some weird and creative Bond gadgetry to intersect with a design like this.

Or maybe Pattinson will arrive on the block with yet another Seamaster Diver 300m, and all of this would've been wishful thinking. But if he doesn't, and this truly is the last we'll see of Bond with Omega, at least First Light introduced one of the better entries in the entire collection.

#3509. Below Deck's Chef Ben Robinson Defends Joao Franco After Arrest

Below Deck’s Chef Ben Robinson is coming to the defense of his costar and friend João Franco after he was arrested in Turkey following a fatal fight.

“I’m so sorry to hear this,” Ben, 45, commented via an Instagram post on Monday, November 16. “Clearly, João was trying to de-escalate the problem. Now he faced five aggressors upon him, and it was clearly self-defense. So unfortunate that this minor lost his life.”

João, 36, and his brother, Karlos Franco, were reportedly arrested in Turkey following a brawl that left a 17-year-old dead.

The pair were seen engaged in a verbal dispute with the employees of a clothing store in the Bodrum district of Muğla on November 7, according to CCTV footage obtained by Page Six.

Although João seemingly attempted to break up the fight multiple times, he eventually appeared to swing a fist at one employee, causing the person to fall to the ground. The fight ended moments later.

The individual who fell to the ground was a 17-year-old employee who hit his head on some stairs, according to local outlets. He later died at a hospital, per the reports. (Us previously reached out to reps for Bravo and João for comment.)

Ben and João starred together on season 4 of Below Deck Down Under, which premiered in February on Bravo.

Colin Macy-O’Toole, who worked with João on season 3 of Below Deck Mediterranean in 2018, also came to his costar’s defense.

“Having seen the video footage, my impression is that João appeared to be trying to defend himself and de-escalate an already escalating situation,” Colin, who was not present for the incident, told Page Six on November 11. “From what is visible, it doesn’t look to me like he was looking to start a confrontation. It looks like he was reacting to what was happening around him.”

Colin, 39, continued, “Knowing João, I think it’s important that people take the full context of the footage into consideration before jumping to conclusions or assigning blame. This is an incredibly tragic situation, and I hope the facts are allowed to come out before anyone rushes to judgment.”

João first appeared on Bravo’s Below Deck Mediterranean season 3 in 2018 as a lead deckhand under Captain Sandy Yawn before returning to the show during season 4 in 2019 as a bosun.

He later appeared on Below Deck Down Under seasons 2 and 4 as a second officer/bosun under Captain Jason Chambers.

Despite the show’s success, João previously announced that he would not be returning to the franchise.

“The show neatly mirrored my real-world career progression. Across the four series, I moved from deckhand to lead deckhand, bosun and finally captain,” he told the Mallorca Daily Bulletin in May. “I never wanted to be a deckhand forever. The goal was always the bridge, so I spent every spare moment doing courses to move up.”

#3508. Civilization Dev Lays Off 1/3 Of Staff, New XCOM Game Facing “Development Struggles” – Report

The video game industry's woes continue as Take-Two's 2K division has confirmed that one third of the staff at Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games is being laid off.

Bloomberg confirmed the cuts, which will impact around 60 people. As part of the downsizing, Firaxis studio head Heather Hazen is leaving.

A spokesperson for Firaxis confirmed the restructuring to Bloomberg, saying the cuts are part of an effort to "focus on design, technology, and player experience."

"These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis," the spokesperson said.

According to Bloomberg's sources, Firaxis is working on a new XCOM game, but it has faced "development struggles" and missed a major milestone this past summer. The game is still going ahead, though the sources said it "may face a shakeup" due to the layoffs.

The latest game from Firaxis, Sid Meier's Civilization VII, was released in February 2025 and had numerous technical issues upon release, though the experience has been improved since then with updates. The entire Civilization series has sold more than 80 million units.

As for the XCOM series, the latest entry from Firaxis was 2020's XCOM: Chimera Squad, and before that was 2016's XCOM 2.

Firaxis was co-founded by Sid Meier in 1996, so 2026 is the studio's 30th anniversary. Take-Two bought the company in 2005 and put the studio and the franchise under the 2K banner.

Maura Higgins became a quick fan favorite on Dancing with the Stars, but I'm worried she could miss the Season 35 finals. With the semifinals and one vote before the finale, I'm afraid her run on the 2026 TV schedule may be at an end. Now, it seems I may have more reason to be concerned about what lies ahead.

On the heels of a tough Grammy night featuring the "Thong Song," it was clear Higgins' rib injury was more than a storyline for DWTS to play up. Now, per a new rumor from The Sun, Higgins allegedly had to cancel a rehearsal and seek medical attention while preparing for Dancing with the Stars' semifinals. Her rib was reportedly re-injured over the weekend, leaving some questions about how she'll be able to perform during the live episode.

As viewers learned in last week's episode, Higgins didn't break her rib, but the swelling and damage caused so much pain that she briefly considered throwing in the towel. It'd be a shame to see, given just how far she's come since the beginning, but obviously, her health takes priority.

As of late, I've written about how Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik's advancement could set up a fan favorite going home instead of them on Semifinals night. Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas were on my shortlist of people who could go home, and honestly, I think it's all going to come down to who gives the best performance.

I Thought I Knew Who I Wanted To Win DWTS Season 35. But One Comment Totally Changed My Opinion

One can never rule out the impact of fans, however, and I do wonder how this rumor could impact their thoughts on whether she should advance. Part of me thinks she could gain sympathy, assuming she wants to keep going, and get the pass to have another week to recover, give it her all, and try to win DWTS on finale night.

Conversely, I could see some viewers deciding it's her time if the performance is weak or if it's evident that she's struggling with an injury. I would see sending her home as more of an act of mercy at that point, rather than putting the pressure on her to drop out of the finale.

All this to say, I'll have all eyes on Maura Higgins as the DWTS semifinals play out. There's so much chatter happening online about who could go home, and this situation is just another layer to consider. I even think there's a possibility that Harry Shum Jr. could miss the finale, which makes the prospect of this episode so much wilder.

Dancing With The Stars airs on ABC and Disney+ on Tuesdays at 8:00 p.m. ET. This is going to be the biggest episode of the season thus far, so make sure to clear that primetime schedule to see what happens!

#3506. Zendaya “Felt Overwhelmed” on the Set of ‘The Odyssey.’ Luckily, Tom Holland Came to Support Her

On the set of The Odyssey, in which Zendaya plays the goddess Athena, there were some particularly challenging days, as the actor recalled during a recent special screening attended by the cast at Los Angeles’s Academy Museum of Motion Pictures. While filming certain scenes—especially those with a crowd of extras—the 30-year-old actor felt “incredibly nervous,” she said.

How did she manage to keep the situation under control? Thank her husband, Tom Holland, whom Zendaya says went to set that day to cheer her up. Spider-Man: Brand New Day star Holland also appears in The Odyssey as Telemachus, son of Odysseus and Penelope. And although he wasn’t scheduled to work at that particular moment, he showed up anyway to support his wife.

Matt Damon’s Odysseus consults with Zendaya’s Athena in The Odyssey.

“I felt overwhelmed, to say the least,” Zendaya said at the screening, as reported by the Daily Mail, with the actor looking stunning in her cream-colored one-shoulder dress, pixie cut, and Christian Louboutin stilettos. “It was interesting because I was on a night shoot, and I remember I came in and I was like, This is like, a pinch-me moment…. I’m in front of these people who I’ve admired, but I’m just like, I don’t want to mess this up.”

While she admitted that these emotions might have worked for her character, they were not so good for her state of mind: “I was incredibly nervous, which I guess is helpful for the scene, but there’s so many other background actors as well who are performing their hearts out—so many—stunt performers who are performing and giving the most beautiful performances.”

The turning point came when Holland stepped behind the scenes to encourage her. “It helped that Tom came to set that day, and he was, like, in the corner like, ‘You got this, you’re doing good.’” It was a team effort.

Zendaya and Holland are one of Hollywood’s most admired couples, not only for their discretion (they quietly married last August 4 in Surrey) but also for the care with which they address sensitive issues, such as mental health. Even in the cult series Euphoria, Zendaya’s character, Rue, grapples with psychological issues—in addition to addiction—as a way to raise public awareness and combat the stigma that often surrounds these kinds of situations.

#3505. How GTA 6 Is Eligible For The Game Awards This Year

We've known for some time that Grand Theft Auto 6 was likely to be eligible for The Game Awards, and now that 2026's TGA nominees are live, it's official: Not only is GTA eligible, but it actually has the most nominations of any game.

That's somewhat of an unusual situation, given that GTA 6 reviews are not yet live. Regardless, this invites some questions of how or why GTA 6 can be eligible before reviews go out and before the game is available. (Nominations even confirmed a key actor in the game.)

For months, the official website for The Game Awards has listed November 20, 2026 at 9 PM PT as the cutoff date for this year's ceremony, which means that any game that launches before that time can be considered for nomination. As GTA VI is scheduled to launch one day earlier, on November 19, GTA 6 is eligible just like any other game already released this year.

Now, before torches are lit and pitchforks are sharpened, evidence suggests that date was not put in place specifically for GTA to be eligible this year: The Friday before Thanksgiving has routinely been the cutoff for TGA nominations.

Last year, the cutoff was November 21, as referenced in this Polygon article regarding Dispatch's eligibility. In 2024, eligibility was cut off on November 22, as evidenced in this Polygon article exploring the games that missed 2024 and were eligible in 2025.

2018 was the last time a Rockstar project was eligible for most categories at The Game Awards, as Red Dead Redemption II landed 10 nominations and four wins. Notably, one of those wins was not Game of the year, which went to Sony Santa Monica for the God of War reboot.

Grand Theft Auto VI's eligibility for TGA 2026 was never in doubt--well, unless it got delayed again. Now that we're clear of that scenario, it's only a matter of time until we see just how many trophies are headed to Vice City.

Pregnant Jen Affleck and estranged husband Zac Affleck are doing their best to be cordial as they prepare to welcome their fourth baby amid their ongoing divorce.

“Zac and Jen are in a good place despite their divorce,” a source exclusively tells Us. “They are coparenting and communication between them has been good.”

Although the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star, 27, filed for divorce from Zac, 30, earlier this month, the pair “talk every day,” according to the insider.

“Zac and Jen are working on baby names, and are really excited to welcome their baby together,” the source says, noting that Zac “will be in the delivery room with Jen and there every step of the way.”

Jen and Zac will “parent together and are still figuring out the plan” in regards to managing their three, soon-to-be four children, the insider adds.

“Jen has asked Zac to continue living together,” the source tells Us, explaining that while the estranged couple are “currently still living together, Zac is looking for his own place and has told Jen that.”

Us has reached out to reps for Jen and Zac for comment.

Jen and Zac tied the knot in 2019, going on to welcome children Nora, 5, Lucas, 3, and Penny, 16 months, November 2021, July 2023 and June 2025, respectively. Jen announced in June that she is pregnant with baby No. 4.

Fans met Jen and Zac on 2024’s season 1 of SLOMW. Throughout the series, the pair weathered a few storms, and they even briefly separated between seasons 1 and 2 of the show.

The former couple relocated from Utah to California in fall 2025 when Jen was competing on season 34 of Dancing With the Stars. They chose to stay after the show wrapped, but their relationship didn’t improve.

News broke on November 3 that Jen filed for divorce from Zac in Utah, where they got married.

“The same reason why I filed for divorce is the same reason why it was really hard,” Jen exclusively told Us on November 10. “It was this fourth child. I had to ask myself very hard questions like, ‘Is this the type of relationship I want this child to look up to?’”

She confessed, “When I realized it was a no, that’s when I realized that I needed to make a change.”

Fans have gotten even more insight into the pair’s split since Hulu spinoff Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County premiered earlier this month.

“Someone came to Zac’s parents’ house yesterday and was trying to serve him papers,” Jen told the cameras. “They were looking for him and he was like, ‘Remember we lived in that home in Arizona? I guess I didn’t pay all the extra charges for us to move out.’”

Jen claimed that after feeling uneasy about the situation — and feeling like Zac wasn’t being truthful — she checked their bank and “the money is gone.”

“There was over $100,000 in there. He’s done this before multiple times — whether it was through online poker or it was through investing crypto,” she alleged. “I said, ‘You’re not allowed to do that anymore.’ Because he’s done this multiple times.”

The source exclusively tells Us that Zac allegedly lost only $60,000 from day trading, noting, “Jen and Zac have never been in a position where they have been financially unstable.”

The insider adds, “Zac had been pursuing medical school and stepped back to support Jen’s career” before their breakup.

#3503. This Fighting Game Is Nominated For A TGA Despite Development Shutting Down

Earlier today, Geoff Keighley announced all of the nominees for The Game Awards 2026, the annual celebration of gaming held in Los Angeles. Among expected nominees Grand Theft Auto VI, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and Control Resonant was one surprising name: 2XKO has been nominated for Best Fighting Game, despite Riot Games announcing the end of the game's lifecycle earlier this year.

Riot announced that "active development" for the fighting game, featuring characters from League of Legends, would end in December 2026. "Over the last few months, we’ve been monitoring 2XKO’s trajectory closely, and what we’ve seen is painting a clear, consistent picture," Riot said at the time. "While a lot of you jumped in to try the game and there’s an incredible community that plays every day, we haven’t seen enough players stick with the game to get to a path toward sustainability,”

Riot's fighter is joined in the Best Fighting Game category by Invincible Vs., Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls, Avatar Legends, and My Hero Academia: All's Justice. 2XKO is also not the only game on this list whose future is in jeopardy; soon after it launched in April, Invincible Vs. developer Quarter up laid off reportedly 75% of its staff, while saying that future updates were dependent on the game's overall sales.

Grand Theft Auto VI received the most nominations for a single game at this year's ceremony with eight, including Game of the Year. Control Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem tied for the second-most nominations with six each, while Phantom Blade Zero rounded out the top three with five nominations. Nintendo earned the most nominations for a single publisher, meanwhile, with 12 across the event's 30 awards.

The Game Awards is set to take place December 10 live from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, California.

#3502. BioWare Is Dead, But Mass Effect’s Spiritual Successor Exodus Just Gave Us A Glimpse of A Spicy Romance

For the first time since its announcement during December 2023's The Game Awards, players are getting a look at the female player-character from its upcoming sci-fi RPG Exodus--which was full of Mass Effect DNA back when we previewed it in September.

The default female version of main character Jun Aslan was revealed today via a seven-minute featurette showing off both female-Jun's face and a bit more of the game itself. The trailer also provided a glimpse of a brief romance scene between female-Jun and Suliman, who is one of the game's romanceable NPCs.

When GameSpot previewed the game, only male-Jun was playable, and we didn't get a chance to romance Suliman, but we did manage to earn his approval, suggesting he may be into both masculine and feminine Jun. We also didn't see the character creator, but there certainly appears to be one, as we see Jun sporting a different look during the romantic encounter with Suliman, with voice actress Carina Corti (Mafia: The Old Country, Little Death) providing Jun's voice throughout both scenes.

Jun's male character model recently got a complete makeover after players complained his original look wasn't pleasing to the eye, but up until today, it wasn't clear who was voicing him. Today, Archetype shared that Stephen Oyoung (Marvel's Spider-Man, Marvel's Spider-Man 2) will be voicing the character.

The female-Jun reveal is followed by a featurette called Scrappy Salvager, featuring a behind-the-scenes look at Jun's origins and the way players' decision can impact Jun's trajectory early on in the game.

"We think of players as the co-authors of our story, and that applies to Jun as well," game director Chris King explains in the video. 

Art director Mark Anderson describes Jun as a "little fish in a really big pond," rather than starting off as a typical hero ready to save the world. Additionally, the featurette goes into more detail about Jun's "precognition" ability, which allows them to see glimpses of possible futures. If interpreted correctly, these premonitions may help players make choices that benefit them. But misunderstanding them may lead to consequences that expand far beyond Jun and their friends. Due to the way the game's time dilation mechanic works, player choices can have unexpected effects that impact civilizations for centuries.

After the death of BioWare, it seems the Mass Effect formula will live on in Exodus, with its vast worlds, strange alien races, NPC romances, and narrative choices. It shouldn't come as a surprise, of course--Exodus developer Archetype Entertainment was founded in 2019 by BioWare veterans James Ohlen, Drew Karpshyn, and Chad Robertson.

Exodus launches on April 7, 2027 and is available to wishlist now on the PlayStation Store, Xbox Store, Steam, and the Epic Games Store.

#3501. Glenn Close Gets Teary-Eyed as She Finally Gets Her Oscar at the Governors Awards

The day before the Governors Awards, a studio executive who had attended the past few years told me that she often found herself crying at the star-studded gala. The annual awards ceremony, held by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, is often an emotional event, with honorary Oscar statuettes bestowed on influential figures in the film industry. A tribute to Michael J. Fox in 2022 and a posthumous honor for Quincy Jones in 2024 left many guests misty-eyed.

At Sunday’s gala, that teary-eyed trend continued when Glenn Close finally got to hold her own Oscar, after eight nominations without a win. Others got emotional when Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler, the independent producers from Killer Films, were honored for their tireless work making boundary-pushing and challenging movies. And when Floyd Norman, the 91-year-old artist who was the first Black animator to join Walt Disney Animation Studios, thanked his wife and five children, the crowd cheered along with him. Even though honoree Ridley Scott couldn’t attend, he dedicated his award to his late brother Tony Scott in a video message. “It is about time we all saw him with an Academy Award in his hand,” said Matt Damon in his remarks for Scott, who has been nominated for four Oscars but has never won competitively.

The presentation of honorary Oscars is often a way to correct Academy Award history, recognizing those who have been overlooked but deserve to be honored for their lifetime of dedication to storytelling and film. The Governors Awards ceremony is also a major stop on the Oscar season campaign trail, with a room packed full of stars and filmmakers from the year’s contenders.

This year that meant a surprising number of couple contenders, including Monica Barbaro and Andrew Garfield (who both star in Artificial), Carrie Coon and Tracy Letts (The Liberation), and Zendaya and Tom Holland. Though Zendaya and Holland arrived together and walked through the Ray Dolby Ballroom as a pair, they actually sat at different tables—Zendaya at the Dune table, with Timothée Chalamet and director Denis Villeneuve, and Holland at the Odyssey table, with director Christopher Nolan. Chalamet also made a date night out of the event, bringing Kylie Jenner with him.

The room held a mix of A-list Hollywood stars, like Tom Cruise (in support of Digger), Julianne Moore (The Debut), and Charlize Theron (The Odyssey), and breakout filmmakers of the year, like Obsession’s Curry Barker, La Bola Negra’s Los Javis, and Club Kid’s Jordan Firstman.

Another breakout of the season, La Bola Negra star Guitarricadelafuente, has been busy promoting the film as both an actor and a musician, having written the original song “La Nieve.” I wondered if he was exhausted from doing double duty. “I’m not tired,” he said with a smile, raving that he had enjoyed meeting many of the other songwriters in the race this year.

All four of the presenters who handed the Oscars to the honorees are also in the Oscar race this year. Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother star Mahershala Ali honored Norman; Wild Horse Nine star John Malkovich honored his Dangerous Liaisons costar Close; Julianne Moore, teaming up with Todd Haynes, honored Vachon and Koffler; and Damon, the star of The Odyssey, honored Scott.

As Close took the stage to accept the award from Malkovich, she wiped tears away from her eyes. The star of films including Fatal Attraction, 101 Dalmatians, The Wife, Albert Nobbs, and The Big Chill spoke about being raised in a religious cult and how, in her childhood, animated films were her only escape. She also spoke about being nominated for eight Oscars over her career, insisting that it didn’t phase her not to emerge victorious. “As an outsider, I have never worried about whether I was going to win or not,” she says. “I have always felt that the great honor is to be in the room.”

She wrapped up her speech with a strong statement against AI. “The craft of acting and of great storytelling has never been more vital to the existence of our fragile, violent, but capable-of-transcendence species,” she said. “We are not machines. We are flawed. Our imperfections are our salvation.”

Vachon and Koffler have been making indie films through Killer Films since 1995, championing movies like Far From Heaven, Boys Don’t Cry, Kids, Carol, and Still Alice (which won Moore her Academy Award for lead actress). They dedicated their awards to the many people they’d worked with over the years, some of whom were in the room. “We have walked into propellers with you and what has resulted is usually a piece of work that has touched somebody. Sometimes it’s seen by millions of people and sometimes it’s seen by tens of people,” said Vachon. “But our movies came to life and made it to the screen because writers and directors trusted us with their stories and actors knew we were creating an environment that enabled them to give their best performance.”

Many of the honorees spoke about the mentors and industry giants who had helped them along the way. Close said she’d promised her World According to Garp director, George Roy Hill, that she’d thank him if she ever won an Oscar. “I never got the chance to thank the man who put me in my first movie. Now I can,” she said, holding her statuette up high. Scott, the director whose prolific career output includes Thelma & Louise, Gladiator, Black Hawk Down, Alien, Blade Runner, and The Martian, told a story in his video message about making his brother star in his very first project, the 1965 short film Boy and Bicycle. “I’m flattered and proud to accept this award, but I also accept it for Tony,” Scott said of his brother, who died in 2012. “His great work would certainly have earned this recognition.”

#3500. Court to Hear Christa Pike's Challenge to her 'Indefinite Isolation' in Prison

After Christa Pike’s attorneys challenged her current prison conditions following her failed execution, a federal court is set to hear arguments in the case.

In an emergency motion filed October 30, Pike’s attorneys called on the court to enforce the terms of a 2024 settlement agreement that ended her 28 years in solitary confinement as the only woman on Tennessee’s death row, allowing for her to have group meals, engage in work and other social and recreational activities.

Pike’s attorneys argued in the filing that the Tennessee Department of Correction is wrongly “holding Ms. Pike in indefinite isolation in the prison infirmary,” away from other women in custody, in violation of that agreement.

In a response filed November 4 viewed by Us, Tennessee Attorney General Jonathan Skrmetti argued the court should deny Pike’s emergency motion, writing prison officials have a “constitutional duty to offer medical care to Pike” and “she can be discharged from the infirmary when medically appropriate.”

A judge will hear the opposing arguments from Pike’s legal team and the state on December 1, according to a Friday, November 13, court order.

Pike, 50, who was sentenced to death at the age of 20 after she was convicted of killing her classmate Colleen Slemmer in January 1995, survived two injections of pentobarbital during a botched execution and was taken to a hospital on September 30.

Following her hospital discharge on October 9, her attorneys contend she’s remained wrongly separated from other women receiving medical care at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center as she continues to recover.

In a November 6 reply to the state, Pike’s attorneys wrote, “[The Tennessee Department of Correction] cannot botch the execution of Christa Pike and then point to the injuries it caused as the reason Defendants no longer must honor their Settlement Agreement with her.”

“The Agreement guarantees Ms. Pike group meals, work, lobby time, religious services, and recreation. Defendants do not and cannot deny that they have failed to provide these since at least October 9th. The breach is clear, uncontested, and causing daily harm,” the filing continues.

The state contends in its response to Pike’s emergency motion that it’d be premature to transfer Pike to a separate housing area with other inmates in the prison’s infirmary due to her medical needs and designation as a maximum security incident.

In the state’s response, Skrmetti noted Pike once allegedly tried to kill another inmate and faced discipline for an alleged prison escape attempt. He argued that if she were to rejoin others in custody, it could jeopardize other inmates’ safety.

The attorney general wrote that prison officials “have not breached” the 2024 settlement agreement, “and Pike is not entitled to dictate the terms of her medical treatment and housing.”

The order scheduling the December 1 hearing on Pike’s emergency motion doesn’t indicate whether Pike will appear in court.

Pike’s attorneys didn’t immediately respond to an inquiry from Us on Tuesday, November 17.

Back in August, the public was devastated to learn that actress Hayden Panettiere died at age 36. This was a huge shock, especially considering her brother died just a few years earlier. Clearly this was a complicated situation, which might explain why Hayden Panettiere's mother ultimately decided not to attend her funeral. Folks were thrilled when she reprised her role as Kirby Reed in Scream VI, with Panettiere thanking fans who "came to her rescue". Clearly she's someone who meant a great deal to her fans, many of whom are still processing her death. As for Lesley Vogel, she's given an explanation for missing her late daughter's funeral.

Hayden Panettiere's legacy lives on through her various acting credits. Heroes is streaming on Netflix, while Nashville is over on Pluto TV. Our thoughts continue to be with her loved ones as they mourn and grapple with the loss.
